### docs/copilot-documentation/auth-ui.md

```md
# Auth UI — Reference

This document summarizes the authentication UI used across the FireUX mono-repo, its pages and key child components, and how they integrate with the underlying composables and profile/tenant flows. Use this doc for dissemination and as a quick integration reference for tenant projects.

## Table of contents

- Overview
- Pages
  - `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/pages/auth.vue`
- Components
  - `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/components/organisms/Auth/System.vue` (OrganismsAuthSystem)
  - `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/components/organisms/Auth/Authenticated.vue` (OrganismsAuthAuthenticated) — referenced by the system component
- Composables and helpers
  - `useAuth` (firebase auth wrapper)
- Migration / notes

---

## Overview

This separation lets tenants inherit a polished, narrative-driven auth experience while keeping per-tenant onboarding logic in the parent page.

---

Purpose

- Top-level public sign-in page with a branded hero card, contextual copy, and follow-up CTAs stacked directly beneath the auth form. It auto-creates the core profile on first sign-in (falling back to the CTA if provisioning fails).
- Shows ecosystem and tenant context using `useFireUXConfig()` (ecosystem, appName, role, appId) to populate the badge, hero text, and feature list.
- Embeds `OrganismsAuthSystem` with `redirect-on-success` disabled and `show-authenticated-card="false"` so the page can present the post-auth CTAs directly below the form.
- After the user signs in and `useUser()` resolves, the card shows the follow-up CTAs in-place:
  Key local state & handlers

- `isSignedIn` — derived from `useAuth().uid`.
- `coreUser`, `appUser`, `pending`, `ensureCore`, `ensureApp` — from `useUser()`.
- `creatingCore` / `joiningApp` — local loading refs used by the CTA buttons.
- `onCreateCore()` — calls `ensureCore()` and toggles `creatingCore`.
- The hero card background tints itself using the configured `primaryColor` for the current app/tenant.

---

Purpose

- Encapsulates the sign-in UI: provider buttons, email/password form, sign-up toggle, and success panel.
- Handles both tenant (join) and global sign-in behaviour.

Public API

- `redirectOnSuccess?: boolean` (default: `true`) — when true the component navigates to `redirectTarget` after successful auth; when false it emits `signed-in` so the parent can continue.
- `redirectTarget?: string` (default: `/`) — route to navigate to when `redirectOnSuccess` is true.
- `showAuthenticatedCard?: boolean` (default: `true`) — when false the internal authenticated success card is hidden so the parent can control follow-up UI (used by the shared `/auth` page).
- `signed-in` — emitted when sign-in completes and `redirectOnSuccess` is false.

Internal behaviour

- Uses `useAuth()` to access `authState`, `signInWithGoogle`, `signInWithEmailPassword`, `signUpWithEmailPassword`.
- Accepts tenant context from `useFireUXConfig()` and adjusts copy and form behaviour accordingly.
- Renders a clear success state (when `authState === 'AUTHENTICATED'`) via `OrganismsAuthAuthenticated` when `showAuthenticatedCard` is true.
- Renders provider button(s) and a custom email/password form; the default view keeps the lightweight ghost Google button and inline error surface so the parent page can control surrounding messaging.

Accessibility & UX

- Password field includes a visibility toggle in the redesigned layout.

### `OrganismsAuthAuthenticated` (referenced)

---

- Wrapper around Firebase auth flows for sign-in, sign-up, provider sign-in and reactive auth state (uid, isAuthenticated, etc.).
- Exposed functions used by the auth UI: `signInWithGoogle`, `signInWithEmailPassword`, `signUpWithEmailPassword`, `authState`, `uid`.
- `useUser()` (core)

  - High-level grouped user helpers: returns `coreUser`, `appUser`, `pending`, and merges into computed `user` (overlay). Also provides `ensureCore()` and `ensureApp()` helpers used by `auth.vue` CTAs.

  - `ensureCore()` creates a core `users/{uid}` document if missing.
  - `ensureApp()` creates app membership `apps/{appId}/users/{uid}` if tenant-scoped membership is missing.

- `useFireUXConfig()`
  - Runtime configuration accessor that provides `appName`, `ecosystem`, `role`, `appId` and derived flags `isTenant` / `isGlobal`.

---

## Integration examples

```vue
<template>
  <OrganismsAuthSystem
    :redirect-on-success="false"
    :show-authenticated-card="false"
    @signed-in="onAuthSignedIn"
  />
</template>

<script setup>
import { useUser } from 'fireux-core/runtime/composables/fireux/firestore/core/user/useUser'

const { coreUser, appUser, pending, ensureCore, ensureApp } = useUser()

// parent may simply react to the composable refs. Example CTA handler:
async function onCreateCore() {
  await ensureCore()
}
</script>
```

2. Simple standalone use (auto-redirect):

```vue
<OrganismsAuthSystem redirect-on-success redirect-target="/console" />
```

---

## Flows and UX guidance

- For tenant join flows, require a core profile first. The recommended UX is:

  1. Sign in / Sign up on `/auth` (auto-provision core profile via `ensureUser`).
  2. If auto-provision fails, show a CTA to create it (call `ensureCore`).
  3. If tenant and `coreUser` exists but `appUser` missing, show a CTA to join the tenant (call `ensureApp`).
  4. Only after both are present show success and let the user continue.

- When using third-party auth providers (Google), the parent page should typically not rely on automatic redirects; prefer the `signed-in` emit to confirm sign-in and keep the user on the CTA flow.

---

- Page: `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/pages/auth.vue`
- Component: `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/components/organisms/Auth/System.vue`

- If a tenant previously overrode `pages/professionals.vue` or other auth-related pages, mention that the shared module now handles the `/auth` page and that tenant-level overrides will take precedence. To adopt the shared flow, delete or refactor tenant overrides.

- Keep `useUserEnsure` behavior consistent: `ensureCore()` and `ensureApp()` are the canonical helpers for creating the corresponding DB entries.

- [ ] Verify you can sign in with Google and the parent page stays (when `redirect-on-success=false`).
- [ ] Verify automatic core profile provisioning after first sign-in (CTA only appears if provisioning fails).
- [ ] For tenant projects, verify `Join <Tenant>` CTA appears after core creation and calls `ensureApp()`.

- Add a one-page PDF export for dissemination.

Tell me which follow-up you'd prefer and I will add it next.
await ensureCore()

```

### docs/copilot-documentation/copilot-01-orientation.md

```md
---
title: Orientation & Mission
status: draft
created: 2025-10-15
---

# Orientation & Mission

FireUX is an opinionated layer on top of Nuxt 4 + Firebase. Drop in a few env vars, add your branding assets, and you have a working web app with profiles, consoles, and common objects ready to extend.

We are indie and unknown by default, so this chapter explains what FireUX is, why it exists, and how the repo is laid out so you can get moving fast.

This handbook pairs with the GitHub Spec Kit workspace (`.specify/`, `.github/prompts/`). Spec Kit holds live specs and plans; the handbook keeps the durable rules and architecture. When one changes, update the other.

## Mission & Pillars

- **Unified experiences**: ship consistent UX across tenants while allowing each ecosystem to extend or theme the surface area it owns.
- **Source-first delivery**: every package exports `src/` only; builds happen at publish/deploy time so code review always sees the real source.
- **Single configuration path**: one way to compose Nuxt apps (`createFireuxConfig`) and one Firebase entry point (VueFire module) keeps behaviour predictable.
- **Accessible documentation**: humans and agents share this handbook for enduring guidance while Spec Kit tracks active specs and implementation plans.

## Repository Map

| Area                                | Description                                                                                                |
| ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `packages/core/fireux-core`         | Shared components, composables, config helpers, auto-registered UI primitives.                             |
| `packages/extensions/*`             | Optional feature slices (for example `fireux-places`, `fireux-jobs`) that layer on top of the core module. |
| `packages/ecosystem/*`              | Ecosystem bundles that select extensions and contribute tenant-specific pages/configuration.               |
| `projects/<ecosystem>/<app>`        | Deployable Nuxt apps that wrap tenant modules through `createFireuxConfig`.                                |
| `scripts/`, `tools/`, `migrations/` | Automation, data backfills, and guard scripts for repo maintenance.                                        |
| `copilot-documentation/`            | This handbook, appendices, ADRs, and links into package-level docs.                                        |

For historical context, refer to the migration notes in repo history; the previous documentation set was retired on 2025-10-15.

## How to Use the Handbook

1. Start here, then read Architecture → Configuration → Workflow.
2. Use appendices for quick references (commands, env tables, runbooks) once populated.
3. Put package-specific details beside the code under `packages/**/docs/`; the [package documentation map](./package-docs-index.md) links to each location.
4. When behaviour changes, update the matching chapter and link any ADR or package doc so decisions stay traceable.

## Working with GitHub Spec Kit

- Run Spec Kit commands (for example `/speckit.constitution`, `/speckit.specify`) to capture live requirements inside `.specify/`.
- Cross-link Spec Kit artifacts and handbook chapters when a spec becomes a lasting convention.
- Update `.github/prompts/` if command workflows change so agents get the right guidance in-editor.

## Definition of “Done” for Changes

- Code change is covered by lint, type-check, and, where applicable, tests or scripts.
- Documentation is updated in the matching chapter or package doc.
- If the change alters a decision, add or extend an ADR under `copilot-adr/`.
- Related automation (scripts, tasks) is recorded in the development workflow chapter.

Proceed to the [Architecture Snapshot](./copilot-02-architecture.md) for a look at how the platform layers interact.

```

### docs/copilot-documentation/copilot-02-architecture.md

```md
---
title: Architecture Snapshot
status: draft
created: 2025-10-15
---

# Architecture Snapshot

This chapter summarizes the runtime layers, data flow, and ownership boundaries that define the FireUX platform. Understanding these relationships is essential before modifying modules, tenants, or Nuxt apps.

## Layered Structure

- **Core (`packages/core/fireux-core`)** provides shared UX primitives, runtime composables, configuration helpers, and auto-registered components.
- **Extensions (`packages/extensions/*`)** add domain-specific capability (Jobs, Places, etc.). Each extension depends on `fireux-core`, exports its own Nuxt module, and owns the routes, stores, and assets for that feature slice.
- **Tenants (`packages/ecosystem/*`)** compose extensions for an ecosystem (e.g. Misebox). They configure routing, theming, and tenant-specific pages while delegating shared logic to core/extensions.
- **Apps (`projects/<ecosystem>/<app>`)** are Nuxt shells that call `createFireuxConfig` to install tenant modules, provide branding, and host deployment-specific configuration.

## Data & Auth Flow

- Client Firebase is initialised once via the VueFire module bundled inside `createFireuxConfig`. No package should call `initializeApp` directly.
- Server-side Firebase Admin usage is restricted to Nitro handlers and utilities; credentials come from `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` (JSON) or split env vars.
- Collections follow the `core` vs `apps/<appId>` pattern. Core modules read/write to global collections; tenants default to app-scoped collections unless a scope override is supplied.
- Composables expose scoped helpers (e.g. `useUser`, `useFireUXConfig`) that pick the right collection automatically based on the app role.

## Module Install Graph

1. Nuxt apps call `createFireuxConfig({ modules: [...] })`.
2. The helper installs `fireux-core` and shared Nuxt modules (Nuxt UI, VueFire, PWA) and deduplicates additional modules.
3. Tenants register their own module plus extensions they own; they never install `fireux-core` directly.
4. Extensions install `fireux-core` and register their own runtime assets to guarantee availability regardless of which tenant consumes them.

Keep module lists single-sourced: if a tenant installs an extension, the app should not list it again.

## Routing Ownership

- Extensions expose their pages through `src/config/pages-config.ts` (see `fireux-places` and `fireux-jobs`).
- Tenants aggregate routes from installed extensions and add tenant-only screens.
- Apps own shell-level routes (marketing, auth). Avoid re-declaring routes that belong to an extension or tenant.
- Navigation metadata (`definePageMeta({ nav: ... })`) drives the dev layout and should live with the page that exports the route.

## Documentation Boundaries

- Platform-wide behaviour (like the rules above) stays in this handbook.
- Deep dives or inventories specific to a package belong under `packages/**/docs/` and are indexed from [package-docs-index.md](./package-docs-index.md).
- Historical deep dives were removed after the 2025-10-15 migration; use repository history if you need to recover prior context.

Continue to [Configuration & Tooling](./copilot-03-configuration.md) to see how Nuxt, TypeScript, and environment settings are composed.

```

### docs/copilot-documentation/copilot-03-configuration.md

```md
---
title: Configuration & Tooling
status: draft
created: 2025-10-15
---

# Configuration & Tooling

This chapter documents the canonical way to configure Nuxt apps, TypeScript, environment variables, and supporting tooling across the mono-repo.

## Nuxt Composition

All FireUX apps wrap Nuxt config through `createFireuxConfig` exported by `fireux-core`:

```ts
// projects/<ecosystem>/<app>/nuxt.config.ts
import { defineNuxtConfig } from 'nuxt/config'
import { createFireuxConfig } from 'fireux-core'

export default defineNuxtConfig(
  createFireuxConfig({
    appName: 'Misebox',
    appShortName: 'Misebox',
    ecosystem: 'misebox',
    modules: ['fireux-misebox'],
    role: 'global',
  })
)
```

`createFireuxConfig`:

- Installs shared modules (Nuxt UI, Nuxt Icon, VueFire, PWA).
- Deduplicates the module list (extensions can be safely registered by tenants).
- Mirrors ecosystem metadata into `runtimeConfig.public`.
- Applies standard Vite, Nitro, and runtime defaults (FS allow list, auto-imports, color config).
- Accepts `includeCore: false` for exceptional cases where `fireux-core` must be omitted (avoid unless migrating legacy projects).

## TypeScript Setup

- Root `tsconfig.json` sets shared compiler options and path aliases.
- Each app extends the base config and maps package aliases to `src/`:

```jsonc
{
  "extends": "../tsconfig.app.base.json",
  "compilerOptions": {
    "baseUrl": ".",
    "moduleResolution": "Bundler",
    "paths": {
      "fireux-core/*": ["../../../packages/core/fireux-core/src/*"],
      "fireux-places/*": ["../../../packages/extensions/fireux-places/src/*"],
      "fireux-jobs/*": ["../../../packages/extensions/fireux-jobs/src/*"],
      "fireux-misebox/*": ["../../../packages/ecosystem/fireux-misebox/src/*"]
    },
    "types": ["nuxt", "vite/client", "@vite-pwa/nuxt"],
    "skipLibCheck": true
  },
  "include": ["./.nuxt/nuxt.d.ts", "./**/*.ts", "./**/*.d.ts"]
}
```

Notes:

- Keep Nuxt defaults (`~`, `@`, `~~`) untouched so they continue to point at `app/`.
- Prefer public exports (`fireux-core/runtime/...`) over legacy aliases like `#fireux-core-runtime`.
- When adding a new package, update workspace `tsconfig.json` and the relevant app configs to maintain path parity.

## Environment Management

- App env template lives at `templates/.env.app.template` and defines the canonical required keys for every app.
- Ecosystem config type is defined in `fireux-core/config/ecosystem` (public, shared, committed).
- Firebase credentials can be supplied as JSON (`FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`) or split fields (`FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID`, etc.). `createFireuxConfig` normalizes private keys with newline handling.
- Service-account file convention (local dev): each ecosystem keeps an uncommitted service account JSON at:
  - `packages/ecosystem/fireux-<ecosystem>/src/config/firebase/service-account.json`
  - Point `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` at this file to enable Firebase Admin scripts and `/api/app/env-check`.
- Places API access uses `GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY`. The helper exposes it via `runtimeConfig.public.googlePlacesApiKey` for both client composables and server handlers.
- Add new env vars through `copilot-documentation/copilot-appendices/README.md` once populated so they remain discoverable.

## Tooling Quick Reference

- **Install**: `pnpm install`
- **Build packages**: `pnpm build:packages`
- **Type-check**: `pnpm typecheck:packages`, `pnpm typecheck:apps`
- **Lint**: `pnpm lint`
- **Dev servers**: `pnpm dev:fireux`, `pnpm dev:misebox`, `pnpm dev:cleanbox`, or `pnpm dev:all`
- **Guards**: scripts under `tools/` (e.g. `tools/guard-tsconfigs.mjs`, `tools/check-app-structure.mjs`)
- **Project scripts**: see the cheatsheet in `docs/copilot-documentation/copilot-appendices/scripts-cheatsheet.md` (backed by `scripts/`).

Before committing configuration changes, run lint, type-check, and any relevant guard script to ensure shared settings remain in sync across packages and apps.

Next: read about shared services in [Platform Services](./copilot-04-platform-services.md).

```

### docs/copilot-documentation/copilot-04-platform-services.md

```md
---
title: Platform Services
status: draft
created: 2025-10-15
---

# Platform Services

FireUX integrates Firebase, Google Places, and shared media services. This chapter records the canonical usage patterns so features remain consistent across packages.

## Firebase Client (VueFire)

- Client initialization is handled entirely by the VueFire module configured inside `createFireuxConfig`.
- `auth: { enabled: true, sessionCookie: false }` keeps the client slim and compatible with cross-app usage.
- Access Firebase services via VueFire composables:

```ts
import { useFirebaseApp, useFirestore, useCurrentUser } from 'vuefire'
```

- Components such as `<DevAuth />` are auto-registered by `fireux-core` and provide anonymous sign-in for development. Avoid custom Firebase plugins unless the module exposes a shared helper.

## Firebase Admin (Nitro)

- Use `firebase-admin` only in server routes, Nitro event handlers, or background scripts.
- Wrap initialization in a singleton to avoid duplicate app warnings.
- Credentials come from `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` (JSON) or split env vars. `createFireuxConfig` passes the admin block to VueFire when the env set is complete.
- Scope Firestore writes to either `core` collections or `apps/<appId>` depending on the role determined by `useFireUXConfig`.

## Places & External Search

- Google Places requests use `GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY`. The key is exposed to both client and server via `runtimeConfig.public.googlePlacesApiKey`.
- Places domain logic lives in `fireux-places`. Route handlers reside under `packages/extensions/fireux-places/src/server/` and composables under `.../src/runtime/...`.
- Keep Firestore records aligned with Places data using scripts in `scripts/` (for example `2025-10-ensure-place-professional-links.ts`). Run once in dry-run mode (if supported) before applying changes.

## Media & Storage

- Avatar uploads and other media use the shared `useImageStorage` helper in `fireux-core`. It automatically scopes paths to `core` or `apps/<appId>` collections and returns the hosted URL.
- When adding new media types, reuse this helper or extend it in `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/composables/core/firebase` so storage rules remain centralized.

## Observability & Diagnostics

- Logging: prefer Nitro `logger` for server-side messages and `consola` for client-side debug logs. Maintain consistent prefixes (`[fireux-core]`, `[fireux-places]`, etc.).
- Dev tools: `fireux-core` provides dev pages (e.g. `/dev/app` (alias `/dev/apps`), `/dev/users`) to inspect runtime state. When extending diagnostics, add new dev pages under the owning package and tag them with `layout: 'dev'` and appropriate `nav` metadata.
- Future appendices will collect alert destinations and monitoring consoles once they are standardised.

Continue to [Development Workflow](./copilot-05-development-workflow.md) for day-to-day practices.

```

```md
---
title: Development Workflow
status: draft
created: 2025-10-15

# Development Workflow

This chapter describes the standard local workflow, branching expectations, and automation available to FireUX contributors.

## Local Setup

1. Install dependencies: `pnpm install`
2. Run package builds when APIs change: `pnpm build:packages`
3. Launch the relevant dev server:
   - `pnpm dev:fireux` (core showcase)
   - `pnpm dev:misebox` / `pnpm dev:cleanbox` / `pnpm dev:niederhorn`
   - `pnpm dev:all` for multi-app orchestration (long-running background task)
4. Use `.env` values from the root `.env` file (symlinked into project folders). Do not create divergent env files per app.

## Dev env panel

- Location: `http://localhost:<port>/dev` (dev layout landing page). Works across ecosystems; Misebox/Cleanbox keep it job-agnostic.
- Backed by `/api/app/env-check`: validates required client/server env vars, Firebase Admin credentials (JSON, split keys, or service-account file), and brand assets dimensions.
- Panel sections: runtime summary (ecosystem/role/appId/modules), admin SDK status with notes, and optional runtime JSON toggle.
- If status shows `missing`, add the required env keys or provide Firebase Admin credentials using one of these patterns:
   - `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` pointing at the ecosystem convention:
      - `packages/ecosystem/fireux-<ecosystem>/src/config/firebase/service-account.json`
   - Or root env JSON via `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`.
   - Legacy/alternate file path (still supported in some flows): `projects/<ecosystem>/<ecosystem>-app/config/service-account.json`.
   Run `Refresh` in the panel after fixes.

## Temporary debug panels (clipboard-first)

- Prefer the shared JSON debug component `fireux-core/runtime/components/dev/JsonPanel.vue` ("DevJsonPanel") instead of ad-hoc `<pre>` blocks.
- This panel includes a `Copy JSON` action and an expand/collapse toggle.
- For short-lived debugging, place the panel near the top of the page template for faster access while diagnosing UI state.
- Gate it behind `import.meta.dev` and render it inside `<ClientOnly>`.

## Coding Practices

- Keep changes small and scoped to a single feature or fix.
- Run `pnpm lint` and appropriate `pnpm typecheck:*` commands before pushing.
- Add or update package docs in `packages/**/docs/` alongside code changes.
- When introducing new composables or utilities, document usage briefly within the owning package and link from the handbook if cross-cutting.
- Use `ensureDoc` (`packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/composables/fireux/firestore/ensure/useEnsurer.ts`) for new ensure flows; adapters decide targets, payloads, and optional image uploads so storage logic stays consistent.
- For profile pills (professionals/agents), mirror the canonical user fields and the domain subtitle only. Avoid layering new fallbacks or computed decorations without updating this handbook entry.
- Nuxt auto-registers components under `components/` and package `components/` folders; do not re-import them inside `<script setup>` unless a component lives outside the auto-import graph or you opt out intentionally.

## Branching & Reviews

- Branch naming: `feature/<topic>`, `fix/<issue>`, or `chore/<task>`.
- Target PRs at `main`. Rebase frequently to keep CI stable.
- Include check results in the PR description (lint, type-check, targeted tests).
- If a change affects shared behaviour or workflow, reference the handbook section updated in the same PR.

## Automation Toolkit

- Repo automation lives under `scripts/`.
   - Guards: `pnpm guard` runs `scripts/guard.mjs`, which composes checks in `scripts/guards/*.mjs`.
   - Hygiene: `pnpm gitsave` runs `scripts/gitsave.sh` (guarded save + push flow).
   - Maintenance: `pnpm clean` / `pnpm clean:deep` run `scripts/clean.mjs`.
   - App media tooling: `pnpm audit:app-media`, `pnpm sync:app-media-from-public`, etc. map to `scripts/*app-media*.mjs`.
- Prefer `pnpm` scripts over ad-hoc `node scripts/...` so workflows stay consistent across contributors.
- Treat scripts as potentially destructive: skim the file first, and if you add new scripts prefer supporting `--dry-run` + `--apply`.
- Promote repeated recipes into an appendix (see the scripts cheatsheet once it exists).

## Testing Expectations

- Package-level unit tests should live beside the source (`__tests__` directories) when present.
- End-to-end flows currently rely on manual QA in dev environments; note gaps and propose test coverage in the Operations chapter if incidents recur.
- Scripts performing data changes should log actions and support dry runs where feasible.

Next: see [CI/CD & Releases](./copilot-06-ci-cd.md) for pipeline guidance.

```

# CI/CD & Releases

This chapter outlines the expected checks, pipeline stages, and release practices for the FireUX mono-repo.

## Pre-merge Checks

- `pnpm lint`
- `pnpm typecheck:packages`
- `pnpm typecheck:apps`
- Targeted unit tests (when present)

These commands are the minimum required before opening a pull request. Include their status in the PR body for visibility.

## Pipeline Stages (proposed)

1. **Install**: `pnpm install` with workspace pruning to validate dependency graph.
2. **Lint & Type**: run the commands above to catch structural or typing issues early.
3. **Build**: `pnpm build:packages` plus `pnpm nuxi build <app>` for each deployable app in scope.
4. **Assets & Upload** (future): push build artefacts to the hosting provider or package registry.
5. **Deploy** (future): trigger environment-specific deployments (preview → staging → production).

Document any deviations (e.g., app-specific build steps) in package docs and reference them here when pipeline automation catches up.

## Release Strategy

- `main` is the source of truth. Tag releases using `vYYYY.MM.DD-<descriptor>` once deployment automation is in place.
- Tenant apps should inherit versioning from the platform; avoid per-tenant version numbers unless an external system requires it.
- Record notable release changes in the package docs or Operations chapter (e.g., new migrations, infra changes).

## Rollbacks & Hotfixes

- Keep the previous deployment artefact available for rollback.
- Hotfix branches should fork from the tagged release commit, receive minimal changes, and merge back to `main` after deployment.
- Update this chapter with provider-specific rollback steps once deployment tooling is standardised.

## Outstanding Work

- Automate lint/type/build via CI (currently manual).
- Define deployment providers, secrets storage, and promotion rules.
- Add monitoring hooks to confirm deploy health (see Operations chapter).

Next: review UX guidelines in [UX & Component Conventions](./copilot-07-ux-conventions.md).

```

---
title: UX & Component Conventions
status: draft
created: 2025-10-15

# UX & Component Conventions

Consistency across tenants depends on shared patterns for components, copy, and navigation. Use this chapter as the design contract when building or reviewing UI.

## Naming & Structure

- Components use `PascalCase` with descriptive prefixes (e.g. `MoleculesFormsFirestoreSimpleField.vue`, `OrganismsAppCardsPill.vue`).
- Composables follow the `useThing.ts` convention and live beside their feature.
- Server routes adopt `<name>.<method>.ts` (`example.get.ts`).
- Place CSS in `<component>.vue` using `<style scoped>` unless shared tokens are required.

## Design System

- Core UI relies on Nuxt UI primitives extended by `fireux-core` components.
- State visual hierarchy: atoms → molecules → organisms. Keep molecules focused on layout/behaviour, and let organisms orchestrate multiple molecules.
- Iconography uses the Lucide icon set. Reference icons via `i-lucide-*` class names.
- Utilize shared spacing and typography tokens defined in `fireux-core/src/runtime/assets/styles`.

## Tenant Color Cheat Sheet

Keep `.env` values and `app.config.ts` tokens aligned so Nuxt UI themes match deploy previews. Use the table below when provisioning new environments or validating colour changes.

| App               | Config Primary Token | `.env` `APP_PRIMARY_COLOR` | Config Neutral Token | `.env` `APP_NEUTRAL_COLOR` |
| ----------------- | -------------------- | -------------------------- | -------------------- | -------------------------- |
| FireUX App        | `yellow`             | `#EAB308`                  | `zinc`               | `#71717A`                  |
| Misebox App       | `misebox`            | `#ABB684`                  | `slate`              | `#64748B`                  |
| Niederhorn        | `violet`             | `#8B5CF6`                  | `zinc`               | `#71717A`                  |
| Cleanbox App      | `blue`               | `#3B82F6`                  | `gray`               | `#6B7280`                  |
| Richies Reinigung | `blue`               | `#3B82F6`                  | `gray`               | `#6B7280`                  |
| Tenant            | `blue`               | `#3B82F6`                  | `zinc`               | `#71717A`                  |

Notes:

- Misebox’s custom palette lives in `projects/misebox/misebox-app/app/assets/styles/main.css`; keep the `.env` value on the `500` shade unless product signs off on a new midpoint.
- Nuxt UI defaults (see `fireux-core/src/config/fireux/config-validation.ts`) define the standard hex mapping; when new tokens are introduced, add them there first, then mirror the value in `.env`.

## Forms & Validation

- Prefer `MoleculesFormsFirestoreSimpleField` for single-value Firestore fields in settings-style layouts.
- Use validation and formatting hooks provided by composables (`validateDisplayName`, `formatHandle`, etc.).
- Align actions inline with controls (edit/save/cancel buttons) to reduce vertical sprawl.
- Surface errors via the component `error` prop instead of custom alerts.

## Alignment

Use the FireUX definition of alignment as the default review lens for UI/data changes:

- [FireUX alignment (canon)](./copilot-appendices/fireux-alignment.md)

## Navigation & Layouts

- Pages that should appear in the dev layout must set `layout: 'dev'` and include `nav` metadata with `key`, `label`, `group`, and `layouts: ['dev']`.
- Groups currently in use: `core`, `misebox`, `ext`, `app`. Introduce new groups only when necessary and document them in package docs.
- Production-facing navigation is driven by tenant-specific configurations; ensure the responsible package owns the nav definition.

## Copy & Accessibility

- Use sentence case for headings and button labels by default.
- Provide `aria-label` or `aria-describedby` when icons or non-text controls are used.
- Ensure colour usage meets contrast guidelines; rely on design tokens instead of hardcoded hex values.
- Document microcopy or terminology changes in the relevant package docs so tenants stay aligned.

Proceed to [Operations & Troubleshooting](./copilot-08-operations.md) for support and incident guidance.

```

---
title: Operations & Troubleshooting
status: draft
created: 2025-10-15

# Operations & Troubleshooting

This chapter captures operational procedures, debugging tips, and the baseline incident response flow. Expand it as new playbooks emerge.

## Incident Response Primer

1. **Triage**: Confirm scope (single tenant vs global) and gather logs (Nitro, browser console, Firebase). Use dev pages to reproduce quickly.
2. **Stabilise**: Roll back, toggle feature flags, or revert recent deployments if necessary.
3. **Communicate**: Record the issue in the shared tracker and notify stakeholders (Slack/Teams channel TBD).
4. **Mitigate**: Apply a hotfix branch or data correction script. See CI/CD chapter for hotfix workflow.
5. **Document**: Update this chapter or relevant appendices with remediation steps, then schedule follow-up work (tests, automation).

## Common Issues & Fixes

- **Firebase auth already initialised**: remove custom client init; rely on VueFire module.
- **Missing env variables**: ensure the root `.env` is up to date and symlinked into apps.
- **Firestore permission errors**: confirm collection path matches `core` vs `apps/<appId>` convention and that service account roles include required scopes.
- **Navigation mismatch**: check that the owning package exports the route and nav metadata; rerun `tools/check-app-structure.mjs` if necessary.

## Diagnostics Toolkit

- **Dev pages**: `/dev/app` (alias `/dev/apps`), `/dev/users`, `/dev/fireux-core`, `/dev/fireux-places` (when available) provide snapshots of runtime state.
- **Automation**: Remediation scripts live under `scripts/` (maintenance, migrations, guards). Stick to dry runs first (when supported), then rerun with `--apply` or similar flags once reviewed.
- **Guards**: `pnpm guard` runs repo checks (backed by `scripts/guard.mjs` and `scripts/guards/*.mjs`).
- **Logging**: Use consistent prefixes in server/client logs to trace issues (`[fireux-core]`, `[fireux-places]`, etc.).
- **Analytics**: Pending integration. When added, document consoles and alert policies here.

## Operational Checklists (to be expanded)

- Pre-deploy verification (lint, type, build, smoke tests).
- Post-deploy monitoring (errors, performance metrics, Places API quota).
- Backup & recovery (Firestore export schedule, storage backups).

Additional detailed runbooks should live under `copilot-appendices/` once authored.

```

# ADR-0001 — Nuxt Config Simplification

**Decision**: Apps use `createFireuxConfig` directly; `createBaseNuxtConfig` has been removed from core.

**Why**: One source of truth reduces drift, simplifies imports, and avoids accidental overrides.

**Consequences**: Per-app tweaks happen via options or per-package modules, not bespoke base config wrappers.

# ADR-0002 — Src-first Packaging

**Decision**: Packages export from `src/` via `package.json#exports`. No `dist/` committed.

**Why**: Faster iteration, fewer mismatches between types and code.

**Consequences**: Tooling must respect subpath exports; app tsconfigs may include path fallback for DX. CI builds can still compile when publishing.

# ADR-0003 — VueFire Owns Client Auth Init

**Decision**: VueFire (nuxt-vuefire) initializes Firebase client Auth (with SSR). Custom plugins must not initialize again.

**Why**: Prevent `auth/already-initialized`. VueFire’s plugin supports SSR hydration correctly.

**Consequences**: Use `useFirebaseAuth()` for access. Any auto-anon sign-in must be user-initiated to avoid conflicts.

### docs/copilot-documentation/copilot-appendices/fireux-alignment.md

```md
---
title: FireUX Alignment
status: active
created: 2026-01-13
---

# FireUX Alignment

Alignment means every layer agrees on responsibility and shape.

Not “everything looks the same”, but these things are consistent across the system:

- Data shape
- Naming
- Ownership
- Direction of dependency

When alignment is good, you can:

- Move faster without re-thinking
- Swap UI surfaces without breaking contracts
- Add a new domain (Jobs, Places, Products) without inventing rules again

## The 6 layers that must be aligned in FireUX

### 1) Model alignment (Firestore truth)

Each domain has:

- One canonical document
- Clear foreign keys
- No UI-specific fields leaking in

Example (Jobs):

```ts
Job {
  id
  posted_by_agent_id
  place_id
  company_id?
  kitchen_id?
  title
  description
  contract_type
}
```

Not allowed in the model:

- displayName
- cardTitle
- avatarUrl

Those belong elsewhere.

### 2) Interface alignment (view adapters)

Every domain exposes one interface:

- useJobInterface()
- useUserInterface()
- useAppInterface()
- usePlaceInterface()

Each interface is responsible for:

- card(raw)
- pill(raw)
- searchText(raw)
- label(raw) (optional)

This is where alignment lives most strongly.

If two cards look the same but are built differently, that’s misalignment.

### 3) Component alignment (dumb sections)

Organisms and sections:

- Do not shape data
- Do not invent fallbacks
- Accept already-aligned props

The Admin pattern is the canonical example:

- Sections are dumb
- Admin.vue orchestrates
- Interface guarantees card shape

### 4) Directory alignment (predictability)

If you see a path, you know what it contains.

Example:

- organisms/
  - App/Edit/
    - Admin.vue
    - Dev.vue
    - Sections/

- composables/fireux/firestore/core/app/
  - useApp.ts
  - mutations/
  - utils/view/

When directory structure mirrors mental structure, it’s aligned.

### 5) Responsibility alignment (who does what)

Quick test:

| Question | Correct owner |
| --- | --- |
| How does this render in a card? | Interface |
| Who can edit this? | Page / orchestration |
| How is this stored? | Model |
| How is this searched? | Interface |
| How is this laid out? | Section / organism |

If the answer is “this file does a bit of everything”, it’s misaligned.

### 6) Domain alignment (Jobs, Places, Users, Apps)

Each domain must:

- Follow the same lifecycle
- Use the same verbs
- Expose the same UI contracts

Jobs should feel like Apps, Users, Products — not special, not clever, predictable.

## What alignment is not

- Not over-abstracting
- Not DRY at all costs
- Not making everything generic
- Not premature optimisation

Alignment is about clarity, not cleverness.

## Rule of thumb (FireUX canon)

If you have to remember how something works, it’s not aligned.

Aligned systems are boring. Boring systems ship.

```

### docs/copilot-documentation/copilot-appendices/migrations.md

```md
# FireUX migrations (agent runbook)

Purpose: Provide a repeatable workflow for migrating Firestore data when runtime models change (drift reconciliation).

## When to migrate

- A runtime model in packages/core or extensions changes shape.
- Dev drift toolbar shows missing/extra fields that should be reconciled into the model.
- We prefer migration over legacy compatibility.

## Inputs

- Dev page URL (e.g. http://localhost:3001/dev/apps) to determine collection + context.
- Drift JSON (copy from Dev drift toolbar).
- Target model file (e.g. packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/models/core/app.model.ts).
- Ecosystem Firebase config path:
  - packages/ecosystem/fireux-<ecosystem>/src/config/firebase

## How to identify the collection + ecosystem

1. Use the dev page URL:
   - /dev/apps → apps collection (core)
   - /dev/users → users collection (core)
   - /dev/fireux-places → places collection (extension)
   - /dev/fireux-kitchens → kitchens collection (extension)
   - /dev/fireux-companies → companies collection (extension)
   - /dev/fireux-jobs → jobs + agents + professionals (extension)
   - /dev/fireux-misebox → misebox-specific collections (ecosystem)
2. Use the drift payload entries:
   - Each item shows id + ecosystem (e.g. misebox-app in misebox).
3. Resolve Firebase auth config from ecosystem:
   - packages/ecosystem/fireux-<ecosystem>/src/config/firebase

## Migration strategy (canonical)

- The target runtime model is the source of truth.
- Migrate data to match the model.
- Remove deprecated/legacy fields once migrated.
- Use safe defaults for required fields:
  - strings: ''
  - arrays: []
  - numbers: 0
  - nested objects: {} with required keys

## Workflow

1. Read drift payload and list required changes:
   - missing fields → backfill with defaults or transform existing data.
   - extra fields → move/rename into correct shape or delete.
2. Inspect the target model to confirm canonical shape and defaults.
3. Implement a migration script under scripts/:
   - Name: migrate-<domain>-<change>.mjs
   - Default to dry-run; only write on --commit.
   - Support --project and optional --app / --limit / --pageSize.
4. Use Firebase Admin SDK with ADC or service account env.
5. Run against the correct ecosystem project.
6. Verify in dev page (drift should clear).
7. Document any follow-up data fixes if needed.

## Example: App media nesting drift

Drift shows:
- missing: media.thumbnail_url, media.logo_url, media.wordmark_light_url, media.wordmark_dark_url
- extra: thumbnail_url, logo_url, wordmark_*_url

Migration:
- Move legacy flat media fields into media.*
- Delete legacy fields
- Backfill required app fields:
  - app_short_name, tagline, short_bio, long_bio → ''
  - join_requests → []
  - user_count → 0

## Notes

- If multiple collections exist in one page (e.g. misebox, jobs), treat each section independently.
- Prefer minimal writes: only update docs that need changes.
- Use batch writes with a safe size (<= 400 ops per batch).

```

### docs/copilot-documentation/copilot-appendices/profiles-model-summary.md

```md
---
title: Misebox Profile Model Summary
created: 2025-10-28
source: AI-generated from overlay/composable refactor discussion
---

# Misebox Profile Model Summary

## Core Idea

We standardize profiles across Misebox with a global + tenant overlay pattern. Every profile offers:

- **Global layer** (Misebox core) for long-term identity.
- **App layer** (tenant overlay) for context-specific state.
- **Flattened view** to merge both when needed by UI/composables.

| Layer                 | Description                         | Example                                          |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| Global (Misebox core) | Persistent identity and portfolio   | "Chef Daniel Watson — Grill & Pastry Specialist" |
| App (Tenant overlay)  | Operational context within a tenant | "Hot Station & Buffet at Niederhorn"             |

## Shared Base (`profile.model.ts`)

- `ProfileBase` defines common timestamps and shared fields.
- `FlatProfile<TCore, TApp>` merges core + app state, optionally exposing `appProfile` where overlays exist.

```ts
// packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/models/core/profile.model.ts
export interface ProfileBase {
  created_at: FirebaseTimestamp
  updated_at?: FirebaseTimestamp
}

type FlatProfile<
  TCore extends ProfileBase,
  TApp extends ProfileBase
> = TCore & { appProfile?: TApp | null }
```

## Chef Profile

Represents craft and day-to-day kitchen assignments.

```ts
// packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/models/profiles/chef.model.ts
interface ChefCoreProfile extends ProfileBase {
  specialties?: string[]
  bio_short?: string | null
  recipes?: string[]
}

interface ChefAppProfile extends ProfileBase {
  station?: string[]
  notes?: string | null
  training_internal?: string[]
}

type Chef = FlatProfile<ChefCoreProfile, ChefAppProfile>
```

## Supplier Profile

Represents goods and services provided to kitchens or teams.

```ts
// packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/models/profiles/supplier.model.ts
interface SupplierCoreProfile extends ProfileBase {
  specialties?: string[]
  bio_short?: string | null
  products?: string[]
}

interface SupplierAppProfile extends ProfileBase {
  categories?: string[]
  notes?: string | null
  training_internal?: string[]
}

type Supplier = FlatProfile<SupplierCoreProfile, SupplierAppProfile>
```

## Professional Profile

Captures career identity for hospitality professionals.

```ts
// packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/models/profiles/professional.model.ts
interface ProfessionalCoreProfile extends ProfileBase {
  specialties?: string[]
  bio_short?: string | null
  health_certifications?: string[]
}

interface ProfessionalAppProfile extends ProfileBase {
  role_tags?: string[]
  notes?: string | null
  training_internal?: string[]
}

type Professional = FlatProfile<ProfessionalCoreProfile, ProfessionalAppProfile>
```

## Agent Profile

Models businesses/restaurants hiring and coordinating teams.

```ts
// packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/models/profiles/agent.model.ts
interface AgentCoreProfile extends ProfileBase {
  specialties?: string[]
  bio_short?: string | null
  kitchens?: string[]
}

interface AgentAppProfile extends ProfileBase {
  departments?: string[]
  notes?: string | null
  training_internal?: string[]
}

type Agent = FlatProfile<AgentCoreProfile, AgentAppProfile>
```

## Firestore Layout

```
misebox-core/
  chefs/{uid}
  suppliers/{uid}
  professionals/{uid}
  agents/{uid}

apps/{appId}/
  chefs/{uid}
  suppliers/{uid}
  professionals/{uid}
  agents/{uid}
```

Each tenant document extends its global counterpart with contextual fields, enabling consistent overlays.

## Benefits

- **Lightweight:** Avoids duplication; each layer owns only relevant data.
- **Consistent:** Identical structure across profile types.
- **Extensible:** Easy to add properties per layer.
- **Composable:** Aligns with new `useProfile`/overlay composables.
- **Multi-tenant:** Clear separation between global identities and tenant context.

---

_Pending:_ Add optional "Kitchen preview" section illustrating Chef ↔ Kitchen relationships with the same global/app pattern.

```

---
title: Scripts & Commands Cheatsheet
status: working
updated: 2026-01-11
---

# Scripts & Commands Cheatsheet

This appendix is the quick map from `pnpm` commands → underlying files in `scripts/`.

## Dev servers

- `pnpm dev:fireux` → frees port 3000 via `scripts/free-port.mjs`, then runs the FireUX app dev server.
- `pnpm dev:misebox` / `pnpm dev:cleanbox` / `pnpm dev:niederhorn` / `pnpm dev:richies` / `pnpm dev:tenant`
- `pnpm dev:all` / `pnpm dev:all-extended` → runs multiple dev servers via `concurrently`.

## Repo guards + save flow

- `pnpm guard` → `scripts/guard.mjs` (composes checks in `scripts/guards/*.mjs`).
- `pnpm pre-guard-clean` → `scripts/pre-guard-clean.mjs` (repo hygiene before guard).
- `pnpm gitsave` → `scripts/gitsave.sh` (guarded save/push workflow).

## Cleaning

- `pnpm clean` → `scripts/clean.mjs`
- `pnpm clean:deep` → `scripts/clean.mjs --deep`

## CTA generation

- `pnpm gen:cta-innards` → `scripts/generate-cta-innards.mjs`
- `pnpm gen:cta-trees` → `scripts/generate-cta-parent-trees.mjs`

## App media maintenance (destructive)

- `pnpm audit:app-media` → `scripts/audit-app-media.mjs`
- `pnpm list:app-media-trash` → `scripts/list-app-media-trash.mjs`
- `pnpm delete:app-media-trash` → `scripts/delete-app-media-trash.mjs`
- `pnpm delete:app-media-folders` → `scripts/delete-app-media-folders.mjs`
- `pnpm sync:app-media-from-public` → `scripts/sync-app-media-from-public.mjs`

## Firestore maintenance / migrations (destructive)

- `pnpm clear:app-fields` → `scripts/clear-app-firestore-fields.mjs`
- One-off migration scripts live as standalone files in `scripts/` (examples: `scripts/migrate-places-canonical.mjs`).

## Safety notes

- Prefer `pnpm <script>` over running `node scripts/...` directly.
- Assume anything that writes to Firestore or Storage is destructive unless it explicitly says otherwise.
- If you add new migration/maintenance scripts, prefer supporting `--dry-run` + `--apply` and documenting flags at the top of the file.

```

### docs/copilot-documentation/copilot-appendices/theming-fireux-apps.md

```md
# Theming FireUX Apps

**Status:** Stable  
**Audience:** App developers & designers  
**Scope:** How to give each FireUX app its own color theme while reusing the shared core design system.

---

## 1. Mental Model

Theming in FireUX has **two layers**:

1. **Core design system** (shared)
   - Lives in `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/assets/styles/main.css`
   - Provides layout, typography, spacing, animations, and more
   - Uses Nuxt UI and Tailwind tokens (`@nuxt/ui`, `tailwindcss`)
2. **App theme** (per app or tenant)
   - Lives inside the app, for example `projects/misebox/misebox-app`
   - Defines a named color palette (such as `misebox`) and tells Nuxt UI to use it
   - Can tweak or override core styles if needed

Core is the base. Apps layer their theme on top; nothing in core is deleted.

---

## 2. Where Theming Is Configured

Each app controls its theme in two places:

1. `app/app.config.ts` tells Nuxt UI which color name to use
2. `app/assets/styles/main.css` defines the actual color variables for that name

Example for `projects/misebox/misebox-app`:

- `app/app.config.ts`:

  ```ts
  import { defineAppConfig } from '#imports'

  export default defineAppConfig({
    ui: {
      colors: {
        primary: 'misebox', // custom palette name
        neutral: 'zinc', // keep neutral aligned with core choice
      },
      safelistColors: ['misebox'],
    },
  })
  ```

- `app/assets/styles/main.css`:

  ```css
  @layer base {
    :root {
      /* Misebox primary palette */
      --ui-color-misebox-50: #f2f4ec;
      --ui-color-misebox-100: #e6e9da;
      --ui-color-misebox-200: #d5dac1;
      --ui-color-misebox-300: #c4cba9;
      --ui-color-misebox-400: #b7c196;
      --ui-color-misebox-500: #abb684;
      --ui-color-misebox-600: #96a074;
      --ui-color-misebox-700: #808863;
      --ui-color-misebox-800: #666d4f;
      --ui-color-misebox-900: #4d523b;

      /* Optional: direct bridges for Nuxt UI tokens */
      --ui-primary: var(--ui-color-misebox-500);
      --ui-primary-hover: var(--ui-color-misebox-600);
      --ui-primary-active: var(--ui-color-misebox-700);
    }
  }
  ```

Nuxt UI will:

- Look at `primary: 'misebox'`
- Read `--ui-color-misebox-*` variables
- Use those values for `<UButton color="primary">`, links, and similar components

---

## 3. How App CSS Loads vs Core CSS

Each app's `nuxt.config.ts` starts from a shared FireUX config:

```ts
import { defineNuxtConfig } from 'nuxt/config'
import type { NuxtConfig } from 'nuxt/schema'
import { createFireuxConfig } from 'fireux-core'

const baseConfig = createFireuxConfig({
  appName: 'Misebox',
  appShortName: 'Misebox',
  ecosystem: 'misebox',
  modules: ['fireux-misebox'],
  role: 'global',
  nitro: {
    firebase: {
      serverFunctionName: 'miseboxServer',
    },
  },
})

export default defineNuxtConfig(<NuxtConfig>{
  ...baseConfig,
  css: [...(baseConfig.css ?? []), '@/assets/styles/main.css'],
})
```

Important details:

- `baseConfig.css` already includes the core CSS from `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/assets/styles/main.css`:

  ```css
  @import 'tailwindcss';
  @import '@nuxt/ui';

  @theme static {
    /* spacing, radii, fonts, etc. */
  }

  .page {
    /* layout primitives */
  }
  ```

- `baseConfig.css` also includes an additive SCSS entrypoint: `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/assets/styles/main.scss`
  - Use it for mixins/utility SCSS that should ship with the design system
  - Keep it free of hard-coded colors; prefer existing CSS variables/tokens
  - Requires `sass` available in the consuming workspace/app toolchain

- The app then appends its own `@/assets/styles/main.css` with `css: [...(baseConfig.css ?? []), '@/assets/styles/main.css']`

This means:

- Core CSS always loads first
- App CSS loads after, so it can define extra CSS variables (such as `--ui-color-misebox-*`)
- App CSS can override tokens (`--ui-primary`, etc.)
- App CSS can override shared selectors like `.page { ... }` if required

Theming is additive and layered, not a fork of core.

---

## 4. Creating a New Theme (Step by Step)

To theme a new app (for example, a new tenant):

1. Pick a palette name
   - Choose a short, lowercase name such as `misebox`, `cleanbox`, `tenant1`, or `brandx`
2. Define the palette in `app/assets/styles/main.css`

   ```css
   @layer base {
     :root {
       /* BrandX primary palette */
       --ui-color-brandx-50: #f5f9ff;
       --ui-color-brandx-100: #e0edff;
       --ui-color-brandx-200: #bad4ff;
       --ui-color-brandx-300: #91b8ff;
       --ui-color-brandx-400: #6b9cff;
       --ui-color-brandx-500: #467fff;
       --ui-color-brandx-600: #3564d6;
       --ui-color-brandx-700: #274ba8;
       --ui-color-brandx-800: #1b3578;
       --ui-color-brandx-900: #11234f;

       --ui-primary: var(--ui-color-brandx-500);
       --ui-primary-hover: var(--ui-color-brandx-600);
       --ui-primary-active: var(--ui-color-brandx-700);
     }
   }
   ```

3. Wire the palette into `app/app.config.ts`

   ```ts
   import { defineAppConfig } from '#imports'

   export default defineAppConfig({
     ui: {
       colors: {
         primary: 'brandx', // must match the prefix in --ui-color-brandx-*
         neutral: 'zinc', // keep consistent with core unless you have a reason
       },
       safelistColors: ['brandx'],
     },
   })
   ```

4. Ensure Nuxt loads the app CSS in `nuxt.config.ts`

   ```ts
   export default defineNuxtConfig({
     ...baseConfig,
     css: [...(baseConfig.css ?? []), '@/assets/styles/main.css'],
   })
   ```
```

This playbook describes the intended backfill flow to sync `apps/{appId}/admin_ids` with matching `apps/{appId}/users/{uid}` membership documents.

Important: the referenced migration script has not been implemented in this repo yet (there is no `automation/` folder). Treat this document as a spec/placeholder until the script exists.

## Verification

After each project run:

### docs/copilot-documentation/copilot-instructions/documentation-style.md

```md
---
title: Documentation Style (Nuxt UI inspired)
status: active
updated: 2025-12-08
---

# Documentation Style — Nuxt UI Pattern

Adopt the Nuxt UI Docs style: concise frontmatter, short intro, task-first sections, and one or two code examples. Keep tone practical and avoid over-engineering.

## Principles

- Mirror Nuxt UI docs: frontmatter with `title` + `description`, clear H1, and a short “why/what/how” flow.
- Prefer one primary path; avoid branching instructions unless tenant differences require it.
- Keep examples minimal (happy path + one edge); link deeper ADRs instead of inlining.
- Cross-link: handbook chapters for canon, package docs for specifics, Spec Kit for live specs.

## Template

````markdown
---
title: <Title>
description: <One-sentence summary>
status: canonical|concept|working
updated: 2025-12-08
---

# <Title>

## Overview

What it is, who uses it, when to choose it.

## Installation

```bash
pnpm add <package>
# or enable in nuxt.config
```
````

## Usage

```ts
// minimal working example
```

## Configuration

Bullet the key options with defaults. Keep to one screenful.

## Examples

- Example 1: core happy path
- Example 2: tenant-specific tweak (if needed)

## References

- Link to related composables/components
- Link to ADRs or Spec Kit items

```

## Writing Rules
- Use present tense, active voice, and short sentences.
- Prefer bullets over paragraphs; keep sections under ~8 lines.
- Use fenced code blocks with language hints; keep inline code for identifiers only.
- If behaviour changes canon, update the handbook chapter and add/extend an ADR.
- If content is temporary, mark `status: working` and park it under `copilot-documentation/temporary-reports/`.

## Where to place docs
- Canonical/shared: `copilot-documentation/` and `docs/**`.
- Package- or tenant-specific: `packages/<scope>/<name>/docs/` or `projects/<ecosystem>/<app>/docs/`.
- Working notes: `copilot-documentation/temporary-reports/` or `copilot-documentation/imported/` when migrating old files.
```

```

### docs/copilot-documentation/copilot-instructions/layouts.md

```md
# Layouts: usage and authoring

Purpose: keep layout naming consistent and avoid app-local overrides. Layouts live in `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/layouts/`.

## Use existing layouts

- Reference by name (file stem), e.g. `layout: 'console'`, `layout: 'auth'`, `layout: 'docs'`.
- Do not copy layouts into apps/tenants; rely on the core exports.
- If you must wrap/override for an ecosystem, do it in the ecosystem package and keep the name unique.

## Authoring rules (core layouts)

- `defineOptions({ name: '<file-stem>' })` — no `Core` prefix; name must match the filename.
- Render pages with `<NuxtPage />`, not `<slot />` — this keeps Nuxt’s page pipeline intact (transitions, middleware/meta, error boundaries, suspense) and avoids edge cases seen with plain slots.
- Keep wrappers minimal; prefer using shared header/footer components rather than duplicating them per app.

## Creating a new layout

1. Add `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/layouts/<name>.vue` following the rules above.
2. Export/register if needed in any module manifest so it’s auto-importable where required.
3. Update docs/nav presets if the layout should appear in navigation.

## Ecosystem/app-specific layouts

- Prefer reusing core layouts. Only add ecosystem-specific layouts when UI diverges meaningfully.
- If you reuse an existing name, you will shadow the core layout. Avoid collisions; prefer a prefix tied to your ecosystem (e.g. `cleanbox-console`).
- TODO: add a guard to detect name collisions and app-local layout directories.

```

# FireUX Jobs — Roadmap

A multi-tenant workforce platform for profiles, job matching, and future on-demand staffing.

---

## Phase 1 — Foundations (Q1–Q2 2025)

**Goal:** Establish the core universal layer for jobs, profiles, and applications.

**Core Deliverables**

- FireUX Profiles (Professional / Agent / Chef / Cleaner / Supplier, etc.)
- Global and tenant profile collections
- Simple job model (title, description, pay range, location, created_by, timestamps)
- Job index pages (global and tenant scoped)
- Job details page
- Job creation flow
- Candidate application model
- Basic application flow (submit application, view applicants, view applications)

**FireUX Packages Affected**

- fireux-jobs
- fireux-core (user and profiles)
- Tenant packages (misebox, cleanbox, future tenants)

**Tenant Extensions**

- Misebox: chef-oriented job types (station, cuisine, tools)
- Cleanbox: cleaner-oriented job types (clean type, building size, schedule)

---

## Phase 2 — Matching Intelligence (Q3–Q4 2025)

**Goal:** Assist agents with smart matching and candidate recommendations.

**Deliverables**

- Basic matching score
- Job filters and search
- Talent discovery pages
- Agent shortlist feature
- Candidate availability and preferences
- AI-generated job descriptions
- AI-generated candidate summaries (profile snapshot)

**Tenant Extensions**

- Misebox: match on station, cuisine, menu types
- Cleanbox: match on cleaning type, building size, timing

---

## Phase 3 — Marketplace Layer (2026)

**Goal:** Enable hiring and job fulfilment through FireUX without acting as the agent.

**Deliverables**

- Stripe Connect (Platform) integration with flexible fee structure
- Secure messaging between candidates and agents
- Booking confirmation system
- Shift timeline (start time, end time, breaks)

**Compliance (light)**

- Auto NDA generation
- Auto service agreement per shift
- Auto invoice templates
- Safety prompts before shift

**Tenant Extensions**

- Misebox: recipe or task list for event prep
- Cleanbox: room or area breakdown for a cleaning job

---

## Phase 4 — Light Compliance System (2027)

**Goal:** Provide semi-automated HR and legal processes without becoming a full agent-of-record provider.

**Deliverables**

- Automated contract generation
- Automated invoice generation
- Tax summary export for workers
- Verified identity and verified agent flows
- Worker ratings, attendance, reliability tracking
- Agent ratings
- Dispute helper (AI-powered)

**Tenant Extensions**

- Misebox: kitchen safety and allergen checklist
- Cleanbox: cleaning standards checklist

---

## Phase 5 — Multi-Shift Scheduling System (2027–2028)

**Goal:** Expand from single-shift jobs to full scheduling and rota management.

**Deliverables**

- Multi-shift job posts
- Weekly rosters
- Worker availability calendar
- Auto-scheduling
- Shift reminders
- AI conflict detection
- Tenant-specific shift templates

**Tenant Extensions**

- Misebox: station schedules (hot, cold, pastry)
- Cleanbox: building rotation schedules

---

## Phase 6 — Workforce Automation Suite (2028–2029)

**Goal:** Equip large-scale hiring teams with advanced tooling.

**Deliverables**

- Hiring pipelines (screening, interview, trial shift, hired)
- Multi-location management
- Team accounts with role-based access
- Automated candidate recheck prompts
- Automated performance tracking
- SLA compliance tracking

**Tenant Extensions**

- Misebox: seasonal brigade planning tool
- Cleanbox: building contract planning

---

## Phase 7 — Payroll and Payment Automation (2029–2030)

**Goal:** Approach full staffing workflows without assuming agent-of-record responsibility.

**Deliverables**

- Time tracking
- Automated pay calculation
- Automated invoicing between parties
- Split payments (agent → platform → worker)
- Expense tracking
- Rate templates
- End-of-shift verification
- AI fraud detection (hours, location)

**Notes**

- Platform remains a payment facilitator
- Stripe handles payout compliance

---

## Phase 8 — EOR-Ready Platform (2030+)

**Goal:** Prepare FireUX to operate as a full temp-staffing powerhouse.

**Deliverables**

- Partnerships with payroll or EOR providers
- Worker leasing solutions
- Automated onboarding and compliance
- Insurance integrations
- Enterprise-grade analytics

**Strategic Vision**

- Cheaper, faster, more intelligent, cross-tenant temp staffing
- The Coople 2.0 opportunity

---

## Tech Architecture Evolution (High Level)

**Phase 1–2**

- Firestore-based profiles
- Per-tenant job collections
- Serverless functions for AI summaries

**Phase 3–5**

- Stripe Connect Platform
- Firestore to BigQuery for analytics

### docs/copilot-documentation/imported/root/create-and-register.md

```md
<!--
source: create-and-register.md (repo root)
imported: 2025-12-08
note: moved from repo root during doc cleanup
-->

# Create & Register System

A shared creation + registration workflow keeps every FireUX asset (apps, modules, ecosystems) consistent, observable, and auditable. This note captures the desired outcomes plus an initial plan for scaffolding, metadata, and storage inside the `fireux-fireux` Firestore database.

## Goals

- One command to scaffold a new **app**, **module**, or **ecosystem** with repo templates, CI hooks, and runtime wiring.
- Automatic registration that writes a canonical record in Firestore immediately after creation (or when promoted from draft → active).
- Consistent metadata schemas so tooling, consoles, and guards can reason about every asset without local heuristics.
- Guardrails that prevent deploying unregistered assets and that surface drift (e.g., deleted repo folder but orphaned registry entry).

## Registry terminology

We intentionally use the word “registry” for two layers of the workflow:

1. **Local registry file** — A `registry.json` (kept next to the asset folder) that contains the full metadata payload. This file is versioned with the codebase and acts as the single source of truth for reviews.
2. **Remote registry database** — The `fireux-fireux` Firestore project, specifically the `<entityType>/<id>` collections (`modules/fireux-core`, `apps/fireux-app`, etc.), where the CLI publishes the same metadata so runtime tooling, consoles, and guards can read it centrally.

The `pnpm registry:*` commands always read from the local file first and then sync to the remote database so the repo history and the database never drift silently.

## Entities & Metadata

Each entity type shares a core envelope plus type-specific payloads. Store all records in Firestore directly under `<entityType>/<id>` so consumers can query by type or aggregate everything (e.g., `modules/fireux-core`).

| Field              | Description                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`               | Slug (kebab-case) derived from the folder name (modules/ecosystems) or the app’s `APP_ID` from `.env` so runtime config and registry stay aligned. |
| `type`             | One of `app`, `module`, `ecosystem`.                                                                                                               |
| `status`           | `draft`, `active`, `deprecated`, `archived`. Guards enforce `active` before prod deploys.                                                          |
| `createdAt` / `by` | ISO timestamp + user identifier (GitHub handle, SSO ID).                                                                                           |
| `updatedAt` / `by` | Managed automatically whenever metadata changes.                                                                                                   |
| `sourcePath`       | Monorepo path (`projects/fireux`, `packages/core/fireux-core`, etc.).                                                                              |
| `runtimeConfig`    | Minimal runtime hints (Nuxt module name, needs Firebase, needs Stripe, etc.).                                                                      |
| `deployTargets`    | Array of environments or tenants this asset ships to.                                                                                              |
| `notes`            | Optional text for ADR linkage, feature flags, or pending migrations.                                                                               |

Lean TypeScript models that mirror the Firestore payloads live under `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/models/core/` (`module.model.ts`, `ecosystem.model.ts`, `app.model.ts`). They intentionally expose only what the registry endpoint persists.

Type-specific additions:

- **App**: default domain, tenant id, enabled modules, storage bucket, analytics ids, optional `ecosystem` slug that points at `ecosystems/<id>`.
- **Module**: Nuxt module entrypoint, auto-registered server handlers, compatible app versions, peer deps.
- **Ecosystem**: list of packaged modules/apps, branding bundle, secrets profile, release cadence.

## Creation Workflow

1. `pnpm create:asset` (umbrella CLI) will prompt for asset type, slug, human name, and optional template. For now we expose dedicated commands per type:
   - `pnpm create:module` → `packages/extensions/<slug>`
   - `pnpm create:ecosystem` → `packages/ecosystem/<slug>`
   - `pnpm create:app` → `projects/<team>/<slug>` and prompts for an optional ecosystem slug (or accept `--ecosystem <id>`).
     Each command writes a `registry.json` alongside the scaffold so registration stays in lockstep.
2. CLI scaffolds files:
   - Apps → `projects/<slug>/` with Nuxt + runtime configs.
   - Modules → `packages/<scope>/<slug>/` with module entry + runtime server/auto-import setup.
   - Ecosystems → `packages/ecosystem/<slug>/` or `projects/<ecosystem>/<slug>/` depending on structure.
3. CLI emits a `registry.json` draft file alongside the scaffold for review and commits it with the new asset.
4. On success, CLI calls `pnpm registry:register --from registry.json` to push to Firestore (requires service creds or uses existing Firebase Admin helpers).
5. CI guard verifies that any new asset folder has a matching Firestore record before merge.

## Registration Flow

- **Command**: `pnpm registry:register <path>` reads the local metadata file, validates required fields, and writes to Firestore (currently `<type>/<id>` using service-account creds or the registry endpoint).
- **Environment**: ensure either `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` (JSON string) or `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` (path) is set before running the command; the CLI reuses the same Firebase Admin bootstrap logic as server handlers.
- **Idempotency**: writes are upserts; the tool tracks `registryVersion` to detect schema drift.
- **Security**: use service account scoped to the registry collection; avoid broad admin keys on developer machines (invoke via existing admin helper + impersonation or a Cloud Function callable).
- **Audit**: store last git commit hash + repo URL for traceability.
- **Notifications**: optional webhook or Slack post summarizing the new/updated asset.

## Ecosystem linkage handshake

- Apps **must** declare an ecosystem during scaffolding (answer the prompt in `pnpm create:app` or pass `--ecosystem <slug>`). Standalone apps are no longer allowed because registry parity is required for every tenant build.
- The registry entry now includes that `ecosystem` slug. When `/api/registry` receives an app payload, it:
  1.  Stores `name`, `team`, and the required `ecosystem` slug at `apps/<appId>`.
  2.  Appends the app id to `ecosystems/<ecosystemId>.apps` via `arrayUnion`, so the ecosystem knows every linked app.
- Future app or ecosystem tooling (consoles, guards, FireUX app directory) can read those lean documents to show "which apps belong to which ecosystem" without crawling the repo.
- If an app later changes ecosystems, update `registry.json` and re-run `pnpm registry:register` so both documents stay in sync (removal logic can run once we track historical memberships).

## Backfilling existing assets

- `pnpm registry:backfill` scans every `registry.json` under `packages/extensions/*`, `packages/ecosystem/*`, and `projects/*/*`, orders them (`ecosystem → module → app`), and posts each payload to `/api/registry` (or `FIREUX_REGISTRY_ENDPOINT`).
- Use `--dry` to preview the sync plan, `--type=<app|module|ecosystem>` to limit scope, and `--include-tests` if you really want to push test fixtures such as `fireux-test`.
- The helper warns when an app entry’s `id` does not match the sibling `.env` `APP_ID` so you can fix the local file before publishing.
- The command reuses the same POST payload as `registry:register`, so audit logs and Firestore history stay consistent.

## Drift Detection & Maintenance

- Nightly job compares repo folders vs registry entries; missing/inactive entries raise alerts in the `guard` scripts.
- `pnpm registry:list` fetches and prints summaries so developers can confirm status locally.
- `pnpm registry:sync` rewrites Firestore entries based on local `registry.json` files (useful after bulk edits).

## Next Steps

1. Define Zod schemas per entity (shareable via `packages/types`).
2. Scaffold CLI commands under `packages/scripts` leveraging existing guard infrastructure.
3. Add CI guard (in `scripts/guards`) that blocks PRs adding asset folders without registry updates.
4. Backfill existing apps/modules/ecosystems with `pnpm registry:backfill` (optionally `--dry` first, then push the real data once the registry endpoint is live).
5. Document the workflow in `copilot-documentation` and link from `server.md` once the API is stable.

```

<!--

# Ecosystem Folder Rename — Before/After Snapshot

## Context

- Change requested: rename the shared tenant package namespace from `packages/ecosystem/` to `packages/ecosystem/` to better reflect the platform → ecosystem → tenant hierarchy.
- Scope executed: physical directory rename plus first-wave config updates so tooling keeps resolving the packages.

---

## Structure Comparison

| Layer         | Before                                                                                                                                                          | After                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Packages root | `packages/`<br>├─ `core/`<br>├─ `extensions/`<br>├─ `tenants/`<br>│ ├─ `fireux-misebox/`<br>│ ├─ `fireux-cleanbox/`<br>│ ├─ `fireux-fireux/`<br>│ └─ `scripts/` | `packages/`<br>├─ `core/`<br>├─ `extensions/`<br>├─ `ecosystem/`<br>│ ├─ `fireux-misebox/`<br>│ ├─ `fireux-cleanbox/`<br>│ ├─ `fireux-fireux/`<br>│ └─ `scripts/` |

---

## Path Inventory — Packages

| Layer                 | Paths                                                                                                             |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Platform core         | `packages/core/fireux-core`                                                                                       |
| Ecosystem packages    | `packages/ecosystem/fireux-misebox`<br>`packages/ecosystem/fireux-cleanbox`<br>`packages/ecosystem/fireux-fireux` |
| Ecosystem tooling     | `packages/ecosystem/scripts`                                                                                      |
| Ecosystem configs     | `packages/ecosystem/tsconfig.json`                                                                                |
| Extension packages    | `packages/extensions/fireux-jobs`<br>`packages/extensions/fireux-places`<br>`packages/extensions/tsconfig.json`   |
| Package-level tooling | `packages/scripts`<br>`packages/tsconfig.json`<br>`packages/tsconfig.packages.tsbuildinfo`                        |

---

## Path Inventory — Projects

| Ecosystem             | Apps / tenants                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| FireUX                | `projects/fireux/fireux-app` (platform marketing)<br>`projects/fireux/tennant` (reference tenant shell)<br>`projects/fireux/tsconfig.app.base.json`                 |
| Misebox               | `projects/misebox/misebox-app` (primary Misebox app)<br>`projects/misebox/niederhorn` (tenant on Misebox)<br>`projects/misebox/tsconfig.app.base.json`              |
| Cleanbox              | `projects/cleanbox/cleanbox-app` (primary Cleanbox app)<br>`projects/cleanbox/richies-reinigung` (tenant on Cleanbox)<br>`projects/cleanbox/tsconfig.app.base.json` |
| Global project config | `projects/tsconfig.json`<br>`projects/tsconfig.projects.json`                                                                                                       |

---

## Shared Asset Targets (Post-Rename Plan)

| Brand layer                         | Recommended shared path                                                 |
| ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Platform (FireUX)                   | `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/public/img/core/brand/*`         |
| Ecosystem (Misebox)                 | `packages/ecosystem/fireux-misebox/src/runtime/public/img/ecosystem/*`  |
| Ecosystem (Cleanbox)                | `packages/ecosystem/fireux-cleanbox/src/runtime/public/img/ecosystem/*` |
| Individual tenant (e.g. Niederhorn) | `projects/misebox/niederhorn/public/img/app/*`                          |

---

## Config Touchpoints Updated

| File                              | Purpose of change                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pnpm-workspace.yaml`             | Updated workspace glob from `packages/ecosystem/*` → `packages/ecosystem/*` so pnpm discovers ecosystem packages.    |
| `package.json` (workspaces array) | Same glob update for npm-style tooling.                                                                              |
| `tsconfig.base.json`              | Redirected path aliases (`fireux-misebox`, `@fireux-misebox/*`, etc.) to the new `packages/ecosystem/...` locations. |
| `.gitignore`                      | Adjusted ignore patterns to track generated d.ts/index files under the new folder.                                   |

---

## Follow-Up Tasks

- Update remaining references to `packages/ecosystem/…` across automation scripts, docs, and guards (grep count was >20). These mostly appear in:
  - Repo scripts (`scripts/`), including migrations and guards.
  - Dev tooling UIs under `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/...`.
  - Documentation (`config-report.md`, project docs).
- After references are updated, rerun guard scripts (`pnpm guard:apps:shape`) to confirm the rename cascades cleanly.
- Shared ecosystem assets live under `packages/ecosystem/*/src/runtime/public/img/ecosystem/`; use each app’s `/dev/images` (or `/dev/img`) route to sanity-check previews before deploying.

---

## Notes

- No package names or import specifiers changed; only the file-system root moved. Existing imports like `import module from 'fireux-misebox'` continue to work because the TS path aliases were updated.
- Ensure any CI/CD or deployment scripts that reference `packages/ecosystem/` are updated before the next release cut.
- Extension packages remain under `packages/extensions/*` (for example `packages/extensions/fireux-jobs`), so no changes are required for that layer.

```
