### scripts/pre-guard-clean.mjs

```mjs
#!/usr/bin/env node
// FILE: scripts/pre-guard-clean.mjs
// Removes local build artifacts that violate FireUX guard L1 shape rules.
// Intentionally conservative: only removes known-forbidden directories at known locations.

import { existsSync } from 'node:fs'
import { rm, readdir } from 'node:fs/promises'
import path from 'node:path'
import process from 'node:process'

const repoRoot = process.cwd()

async function removeDirIfExists(dirPath) {
  if (!existsSync(dirPath)) return false
  await rm(dirPath, { recursive: true, force: true })
  return true
}

async function listChildDirs(parentDir) {
  if (!existsSync(parentDir)) return []
  const entries = await readdir(parentDir, { withFileTypes: true })
  return entries.filter((e) => e.isDirectory() && !e.name.startsWith('.')).map((e) => e.name)
}

const removed = []

// Remove dist/ at package roots: packages/{core,ecosystem,extensions}/*/dist
for (const group of ['core', 'ecosystem', 'extensions']) {
  const groupRoot = path.join(repoRoot, 'packages', group)
  const pkgs = await listChildDirs(groupRoot)

  for (const pkgName of pkgs) {
    const distPath = path.join(groupRoot, pkgName, 'dist')
    if (await removeDirIfExists(distPath)) removed.push(path.relative(repoRoot, distPath))
  }
}

// Remove .data at app roots: projects/*/*/.data
{
  const projectsRoot = path.join(repoRoot, 'projects')
  const ecosystems = await listChildDirs(projectsRoot)

  for (const eco of ecosystems) {
    const ecoRoot = path.join(projectsRoot, eco)
    const apps = await listChildDirs(ecoRoot)

    for (const appName of apps) {
      const dataPath = path.join(ecoRoot, appName, '.data')
      if (await removeDirIfExists(dataPath)) removed.push(path.relative(repoRoot, dataPath))
    }
  }
}

if (removed.length) {
  console.log('[pre-guard-clean] 🧹 Removed forbidden local artifacts:')
  removed
    .slice()
    .sort((a, b) => a.localeCompare(b))
    .forEach((p) => console.log(`  - ${p}`))
} else {
  console.log('[pre-guard-clean] ✅ Nothing to clean')
}

```

### scripts/reset-notifications.mjs

```mjs
#!/usr/bin/env node
/*
  Hard reset: delete notification data everywhere.

  Deletes the `notifications` field entirely from:
    - users/{uid}
    - apps/{appId}/users/{uid}

  Auth (one required):
    - FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT (JSON string)
    - GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS (path)
    - Or Google ADC (gcloud): application-default login

  Usage:
    node scripts/reset-notifications.mjs
*/

import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { promises as fs } from 'node:fs'
import { isAbsolute, resolve } from 'node:path'

const requireFromCwd = createRequire(resolve(process.cwd(), 'package.json'))

async function loadFirebaseAdmin() {
  const adminApp = await import(requireFromCwd.resolve('firebase-admin/app'))
  const adminFirestore = await import(
    requireFromCwd.resolve('firebase-admin/firestore')
  )

  return {
    applicationDefault: adminApp.applicationDefault,
    cert: adminApp.cert,
    getApps: adminApp.getApps,
    initializeApp: adminApp.initializeApp,
    FieldPath: adminFirestore.FieldPath,
    FieldValue: adminFirestore.FieldValue,
    getFirestore: adminFirestore.getFirestore,
  }
}

async function loadServiceAccount() {
  const fromEnvJson = process.env.FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT?.trim()
  if (fromEnvJson) {
    try {
      return JSON.parse(fromEnvJson)
    } catch (error) {
      throw new Error(
        `Invalid FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT JSON: ${error?.message ?? String(error)}`
      )
    }
  }

  const gac = process.env.GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS?.trim()
  if (gac) {
    const path = isAbsolute(gac) ? gac : resolve(process.cwd(), gac)
    try {
      const raw = await fs.readFile(path, 'utf8')
      return JSON.parse(raw)
    } catch (error) {
      throw new Error(
        `Unable to read GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS at "${path}": ${error?.message ?? String(error)}`
      )
    }
  }

  return null
}

async function listAllDocIdsOrdered(db, FieldPath, collectionPath, pageSize = 500) {
  const ids = []
  let lastDoc = null

  for (;;) {
    let query = db
      .collection(collectionPath)
      .orderBy(FieldPath.documentId())
      .limit(pageSize)

    if (lastDoc) query = query.startAfter(lastDoc)

    const snap = await query.get()
    if (snap.empty) break

    for (const docSnap of snap.docs) {
      ids.push(docSnap.id)
      lastDoc = docSnap
    }
  }

  return ids
}

async function listApps(db, FieldPath) {
  const snap = await db.collection('apps').orderBy(FieldPath.documentId()).get()
  return snap.docs.map((d) => d.id)
}

async function commitBatches(db, ops) {
  let committed = 0
  for (let i = 0; i < ops.length; i += 450) {
    const slice = ops.slice(i, i + 450)
    const batch = db.batch()
    for (const op of slice) batch.update(op.ref, op.data)
    await batch.commit()
    committed += slice.length
  }
  return committed
}

async function main() {
  const {
    applicationDefault,
    cert,
    getApps,
    initializeApp,
    FieldPath,
    FieldValue,
    getFirestore,
  } = await loadFirebaseAdmin()

  const existingApps = getApps()
  const hasApp = Array.isArray(existingApps) && existingApps.length > 0

  const serviceAccount = await loadServiceAccount()

  if (!hasApp) {
    initializeApp({
      credential: serviceAccount ? cert(serviceAccount) : applicationDefault(),
    })
  }

  const db = getFirestore()

  const project = serviceAccount?.project_id ?? null
  if (project) console.log(`- Project: ${project}`)

  const userIds = await listAllDocIdsOrdered(db, FieldPath, 'users')
  console.log(`- Users: ${userIds.length}`)

  const apps = await listApps(db, FieldPath)
  console.log(`- Apps: ${apps.length}`)

  // 1) Remove notifications from users/{uid}
  const userOps = userIds.map((uid) => ({
    ref: db.collection('users').doc(uid),
    data: { notifications: FieldValue.delete() },
  }))

  const usersCommitted = await commitBatches(db, userOps)
  console.log(`✅ Cleared users.notifications (writes): ${usersCommitted}`)

  // 2) Remove notifications from apps/{appId}/users/{uid}
  let appMembershipDocs = 0
  let appMembershipWrites = 0

  for (const appId of apps) {
    const subPath = `apps/${appId}/users`
    const memberIds = await listAllDocIdsOrdered(db, FieldPath, subPath)
    appMembershipDocs += memberIds.length

    if (!memberIds.length) continue

    const ops = memberIds.map((uid) => ({
      ref: db.collection('apps').doc(appId).collection('users').doc(uid),
      data: { notifications: FieldValue.delete() },
    }))

    appMembershipWrites += await commitBatches(db, ops)
  }

  console.log(`- App membership docs: ${appMembershipDocs}`)
  console.log(`✅ Cleared apps/*/users/*.notifications (writes): ${appMembershipWrites}`)
  console.log('✅ Notification reset complete')
}

main().catch((error) => {
  console.error('❌ Reset failed')
  console.error(error)
  process.exit(1)
})

```

### scripts/sync-app-media-from-public.mjs

```mjs
#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * Syncs app media from local /public/img/app/* into Firebase Storage and Firestore.
 *
 * Canon:
 * - Storage objects: apps/{appId}/media/{thumbnail|logo|wordmark-light|wordmark-dark}
 * - Firestore fields: thumbnail_url, logo_url, wordmark_light_url, wordmark_dark_url
 *
 * Uses per-ecosystem service accounts from temp/app-media-audit.json.
 *
 * Usage:
 *   pnpm sync:app-media-from-public
 *   pnpm sync:app-media-from-public -- --apply
 *   pnpm sync:app-media-from-public -- --ecosystem fireux-misebox --apply
 *   pnpm sync:app-media-from-public -- --ecosystem fireux --app fireux-app --apply
 */

import fs from 'node:fs'
import path from 'node:path'
import process from 'node:process'
import crypto from 'node:crypto'
import admin from 'firebase-admin'

import { parseArgs } from './_lib/args.mjs'

const workspaceRoot = process.cwd()
const auditPath = path.join(workspaceRoot, 'temp', 'app-media-audit.json')

function stableJson(value) {
  return JSON.stringify(value, null, 2) + '\n'
}

function normaliseProjectSegment(ecosystemId) {
  const raw = String(ecosystemId || '').trim()
  if (!raw) return ''
  if (raw === 'fireux') return 'fireux'
  if (raw.startsWith('fireux-')) return raw.slice('fireux-'.length)
  return raw
}

function candidatePublicDirs({ ecosystemId, appId }) {
  const projectSegment = normaliseProjectSegment(ecosystemId)

  // Known special-case mapping.
  const appFolder = appId === 'fireux-tenant' ? 'tenant' : appId

  const dirs = []

  // Project-level public dirs.
  if (projectSegment) {
    dirs.push(path.join(workspaceRoot, 'projects', projectSegment, appFolder, 'public'))
    dirs.push(path.join(workspaceRoot, 'projects', projectSegment, `${appFolder}-app`, 'public'))
  }

  // Shared/public fallbacks.
  dirs.push(path.join(workspaceRoot, 'public'))
  dirs.push(
    path.join(
      workspaceRoot,
      'packages',
      'core',
      'fireux-core',
      'src',
      'runtime',
      'public'
    )
  )

  // Ecosystem package public.
  if (projectSegment) {
    dirs.push(
      path.join(
        workspaceRoot,
        'packages',
        'ecosystem',
        `fireux-${projectSegment}`,
        'src',
        'runtime',
        'public'
      )
    )
  }

  // De-dup while preserving order.
  const seen = new Set()
  return dirs.filter((d) => {
    const key = path.normalize(d)
    if (seen.has(key)) return false
    seen.add(key)
    return true
  })
}

function resolveLocalAsset({ ecosystemId, appId }, relative) {
  const candidates = candidatePublicDirs({ ecosystemId, appId })
  for (const base of candidates) {
    const full = path.join(base, relative)
    if (fs.existsSync(full)) return full
  }
  return null
}

function randomToken() {
  return crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('hex')
}

function firebaseDownloadUrl(bucketName, objectPath, token) {
  const encoded = encodeURIComponent(objectPath)
  return `https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/${bucketName}/o/${encoded}?alt=media&token=${token}`
}

async function uploadWithToken(bucket, bucketName, objectPath, localFilePath) {
  const token = randomToken()
  await bucket.upload(localFilePath, {
    destination: objectPath,
    resumable: false,
    metadata: {
      cacheControl: 'public,max-age=3600',
      metadata: {
        firebaseStorageDownloadTokens: token,
      },
    },
  })
  return firebaseDownloadUrl(bucketName, objectPath, token)
}

async function main() {
  const args = parseArgs(process.argv.slice(2))

  if (args.help) {
    console.log(`Usage: pnpm sync:app-media-from-public -- [--ecosystem <id>] [--app <appId>] [--apply]

Dry-run by default; pass --apply to upload and write Firestore.
Reads targets from temp/app-media-audit.json.
`)
    process.exit(0)
  }

  if (!fs.existsSync(auditPath)) {
    console.error(`Missing ${auditPath}. Run pnpm audit:app-media first.`)
    process.exit(1)
  }

  const audit = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(auditPath, 'utf8'))
  const ecosystems = audit?.ecosystems ?? {}

  const requestedEcosystem = args.ecosystem ? String(args.ecosystem) : null
  const requestedAppId = args.app ? String(args.app) : null
  const apply = Boolean(args.apply)

  const plan = {
    generatedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
    mode: apply ? 'apply' : 'dry-run',
    targets: [],
    missing: [],
  }

  const expectedAssets = [
    { kind: 'thumbnail', relative: path.join('img', 'app', 'thumbnail.png') },
    { kind: 'logo', relative: path.join('img', 'app', 'logo.png') },
    { kind: 'wordmark-light', relative: path.join('img', 'app', 'wordmark-light.png') },
    { kind: 'wordmark-dark', relative: path.join('img', 'app', 'wordmark-dark.png') },
  ]

  const ecosystemIds = Object.keys(ecosystems)
    .filter((id) => (requestedEcosystem ? id === requestedEcosystem : true))
    .sort()

  if (!ecosystemIds.length) {
    console.error(
      requestedEcosystem
        ? `No matching ecosystem ${requestedEcosystem} in ${path.relative(workspaceRoot, auditPath)}`
        : `No ecosystems found in ${path.relative(workspaceRoot, auditPath)}`
    )
    process.exit(1)
  }

  for (const ecoId of ecosystemIds) {
    const eco = ecosystems[ecoId]
    const projectId = eco?.projectId
    const bucketName = eco?.bucket
    const serviceAccountRel = eco?.serviceAccount

    if (!projectId || !bucketName || !serviceAccountRel) {
      console.warn(`[skip] ${ecoId}: missing projectId/bucket/serviceAccount in audit report`)
      continue
    }

    const serviceAccountPath = path.join(workspaceRoot, serviceAccountRel)
    if (!fs.existsSync(serviceAccountPath)) {
      console.warn(`[skip] ${ecoId}: missing service account at ${serviceAccountRel}`)
      continue
    }

    const appIds = Object.keys(eco?.apps ?? {})
      .filter((id) => (requestedAppId ? id === requestedAppId : true))
      .sort()

    if (!appIds.length) {
      console.warn(`[skip] ${ecoId}: no matching apps`)
```

### temp/agent-job-phase.md

```md
# Agent ↔ Job Phase-1 (Horizontal MVP) — What Exists vs What Doesn’t

Date: 2025-12-28

This note maps the Phase-1 “prove the graph” briefing onto the current FireUX mono-repo models/collections.

## Ground rules from the brief (what we’re validating)
- Horizontal MVP: model *relationships*, not a rich domain.
- Each entity: Identity + linking fields + one “luck” property.

---

## Entity-by-entity reality check

### 1) User
**Brief**: `users/{uid}` with `id`, `display_name`, `avatar_url`; extra: `default_role`.

**Exists** ✅
- Collection: `users/{uid}` (core user doc)
- Model: `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/models/core/user.model.ts`
- Core fields present:
  - `id`
  - `display_name`
  - `avatar` (note: field name is `avatar`, not `avatar_url`)
- Links present:
  - Profiles are linked implicitly by shared UID (`profiles?: string[]` lists profile domains like `agent`, `chef`, etc.)
- Extra “luck” property:
  - `default_role` ❌ not present
  - There *is* `role?: 'user' | 'admin'` and an `appUser` overlay, but that’s not the same intent as “default routing role”.

### 2) Agent (posting authority)
**Brief**: `agents/{uid}` with `id`, `name`, `type`; link `user_id`; extra `verified`.

**Exists (as a profile)** ✅ (partial match)
- Collection: `agents/{uid}`
- Config: `packages/extensions/fireux-jobs/src/runtime/models/profiles/Agent/supporting.ts`
- Model: `packages/extensions/fireux-jobs/src/runtime/models/profiles/Agent/Agent.model.ts`
- Identity present:
  - Uses shared UID via `Profile.id` (optional but standard across profiles)
- Fields present (current Agent profile shape):
  - `title`, `subtitle`, `tagline`, `badges`
  - `bio_short`, `contact_email`, `contact_phone`, `website_url`
- Linking fields:
  - No explicit `user_id` field (link is implicit via shared UID + optional embedded `user?: Partial<User>` from the shared `Profile` shape)
- Extra “luck”:
  - `verified` ❌ not present as a stored boolean
  - There is UI formatting for “verification status”, but it’s not currently modeled/stored.
- Gap vs brief:
  - No `type ('individual'|'company')` field.
  - No explicit `user_id` reference (it’s implicit).

### 3) Company
**Brief**: `companies/{companyId}` (auto-ID) with `id`, `name`, `website`, `logo_url`.

**Exists** ✅ (Phase 1 implemented)
- Collection: `companies/{companyId}`
- Model: `packages/extensions/fireux-companies/src/runtime/models/company.model.ts`
- Firestore helpers: `packages/extensions/fireux-companies/src/runtime/composables/useCompanies.ts`
- Core fields now supported:
	- `id` (doc ID, typically attached by FireUX fetch helpers)
	- `name`
	- `website` (optional)
  - `logo_url` (optional)

### 4) Agent ↔ Company relationship
**Brief**: relationship modeling.

**Doesn’t exist (by design, for now)** ❌
- We are intentionally treating Company as a dead object (identity only).
- Jobs link to company via `job.company_id` and to the posting authority via `job.posted_by_agent_id`.

### 5) Place
**Brief**: `places/{placeId}` where ID is Google Places ID; `id`, `name`, `address`; extra `latlng`.

**Exists** ✅ (strong match, slightly different field names)
- Collection: `places/{placeId}` (the composable expects an ID when fetching a doc)
- Model: `packages/extensions/fireux-places/src/runtime/models/place.model.ts`
- Identity:
  - Uses `place_id` (Google Place ID)
- Core fields:
  - `place_id`, `name`, `formatted_address`
- Links:
  - Google Places API supported via server endpoints under `packages/extensions/fireux-places/src/runtime/server/api/places/*`
- Extra “luck”:
  - Uses `lat` + `lng` (instead of a combined `latlng`)

### 6) Kitchen
**Brief**: `kitchens/{kitchenId}` (auto-ID) with `id`, `name`, `place_id`; extra `type`.

**Exists** ✅ (but modeled differently)
- Collection: `kitchens/{id}` (Misebox ecosystem)
- Model: `packages/ecosystem/fireux-misebox/src/runtime/models/Kitchen.model.ts`
- Identity:
  - `id` exists
  - Comment indicates `id` == `place_id` (1:1 mapping with Places)
- Core fields:
  - `id`, `name`, optional `description`, optional `app_id`
- Links:
  - No explicit `place_id` field because the link is encoded by `id == place_id`
- Extra “luck”:
  - `type` ❌ not present
- Gap vs brief:
  - Brief wants kitchens as a distinct object (auto-ID) that references a place.
  - Current implementation treats kitchen as a place-alias (same ID), which is simpler but less flexible.

### 7) Job
**Brief**: `jobs/{jobId}` with `id`, `title`, `status (draft|live)`, `posted_by_agent_id`; links to agent/company/place/kitchen; extra `source`.

**Exists** ✅ (minimal, but the graph links are mostly missing)
- Collection: `jobs/{jobId}`
- Model: `packages/extensions/fireux-jobs/src/runtime/models/job.model.ts`
- Current core fields:
  - `id`, `app_id`, `created_by`, `title`, `status ('open'|'closed')`, optional `description`
- Links present:
  - `created_by` (user uid)
  - `app_id` (tenant/app scope)
- Links supported (Phase-1 additions):
	- `posted_by_agent_id` (optional)
	- `company_id` (optional)
	- `place_id` (optional)
	- `kitchen_id` (optional)
- Extra “luck”:
	- `source` (optional)
- Status mismatch:
  - current: `open|closed`
  - brief: `draft|live`

### 8) Chef / Professional / Supplier (profiles)
**Brief**: `{domain}/{uid}` with `id`, `name`; link `user_id`; extra `public`.

**Exists** ✅ (as profiles)
- Collections:
  - `chefs/{uid}` (Misebox)
  - `professionals/{uid}` (Jobs)
  - `suppliers/{uid}` (Misebox)
- Models:
  - `packages/ecosystem/fireux-misebox/src/runtime/models/profiles/Chef/Chef.model.ts`
  - `packages/extensions/fireux-jobs/src/runtime/models/profiles/Professional/Professional.model.ts`
  - `packages/ecosystem/fireux-misebox/src/runtime/models/profiles/Supplier/Supplier.model.ts`
- Core fields:
  - All inherit the shared `Profile` shape (supports `id`, `title`, `subtitle`, `tagline`, etc.)
- Links:
  - No explicit `user_id` field (link is implicit via shared UID + optional `user?: Partial<User>`)
- Extra “luck”:
  - `public` ❌ not present

---

## Summary: what the graph currently supports

**Already real (in data model)**
- `User ↔ Profiles` (via shared UID + `users.profiles[]` domain list)
- `Agent` profile exists in `agents/{uid}`
- `Company` exists in `companies/{companyId}` (extension: `fireux-companies`)
- `Place` exists in `places/{placeId}` with Google integration
- `Kitchen` exists in `kitchens/{id}` (currently 1:1 with `place_id`)
- `Job` exists in `jobs/{jobId}` (scoped via `app_id`)

**Already supported (foreign keys exist, even if UI doesn’t use them yet)**
- Job edges: `job.posted_by_agent_id`, `job.company_id`, `job.place_id`, `job.kitchen_id`, `job.source`

**Not yet real (gaps vs the brief)**
- “Luck fields” still missing in stored data: `user.default_role`, `agent.verified`, `profile.public`
- Status mismatch: current job `open|closed` vs brief `draft|live`
- Kitchen link mismatch: brief expects `kitchen.place_id`, but current Misebox uses `kitchen.id == place_id`

If the goal is *exactly* the brief’s Phase‑1 graph, the next minimal delta is to add only the remaining “luck fields” (or explicitly drop them from the brief).
```

### temp/agent-plan.md

```md
# Agent profile strategy (temp)

Date: 2025-12-27

## Goals

- Make the Agent profile **rich** while staying consistent with the existing domain profile pattern (Chef/Supplier/Professional).
- Keep a clean separation between:
  - **membership/role** (AppUser overlay)
  - **domain profiles** (global truth + optional tenant deltas)
- Ensure the Agent can be created/edited by the user via `/console/agent/profile`, and used as a browseable “directory entity” (pill/cell/profile view models).

Agent is a **posting identity**, so “richness” should support:
- trust (“who is this agent?”)
- contact
- scope (“what kind of roles / regions?”)

## Canon data model (do not mix concepts)

### A) App membership overlay (always app-scoped)

- Path: `apps/{appId}/users/{uid}`
- Type: `AppUser`
- Purpose: role/admin, permissions, app-scoped notifications, onboarding.
- Exists for any `appId` (including operator apps like `misebox-app`).

### B) Domain profile (global truth)

- Path: `agents/{uid}` (canonical; keep it aligned with other profiles)
- Type: `AgentProfile` (core doc)
- Purpose: canonical Agent identity and domain data.

Note: avoid introducing `agents/{agentId}` until we actually need multi-agent org constructs.

### C) Tenant profile overlay (tenant deltas)

- Path: `apps/{tenantAppId}/agents/{uid}`
- Type: `AgentAppProfile` (overlay doc)
- Purpose: tenant-specific deltas (visibility, local badges/labels/settings).
- Read/write only when `isTenant === true` (unless explicitly admin-fetched by a target app id).

## Model “shape” conventions (match other domains)

### Domain wrapper (hydrated state)

- `Agent` wrapper is the composable-facing object:
  - `user`: canonical `User` pill (display name, avatar)
  - `core`: `AgentProfile | null`
  - `app`: `AgentAppProfile | null`

### Firestore-facing profile types

- `AgentProfile` = core doc shape (`agents/{uid}`)
- `AgentAppProfile` = overlay doc shape (`apps/{appId}/agents/{uid}`)

### UI view models belong in `useAgentInterface`

- Pills / Cells / Profile-card shapes should be produced by `useAgentInterface` (like `useAppInterface`, `useUserInterface`), not embedded as shared props in the model.
- This keeps model files “shape-first” and view-model logic centralized.

## Minimal “rich” Agent surface (phased)

### Phase 1 (already in motion / baseline)

- Contact + identity:
  - `bio_short`
  - `contact_email`
  - `contact_phone`
  - `website_url`
- Basic branding:
  - `title`, `subtitle`, `tagline`, `badges`

### Phase 2 (richness without overfitting)

- Add structured, reusable fields consistent with other profiles:
  - `specialties: string[]`
  - `locations: string[]`
  - `languages: string[]`
  - `links` (structured social links)
  - `portfolio` (lightweight array of items)

Principle: prefer arrays + simple objects, avoid deep nesting until needed.

## Composables plan (align with core patterns)

### Required

- `useAgent()` orchestrator (keep it thin)
  - hydrates and exposes: `agent` (wrapper), raw refs, `pending`
  - delegates view models to `useAgentInterface`
  - delegates writes to `useAgentUpdate`
  - delegates creation/ensure to `useAgentCreate` / `useProfileEnsure`

Guardrail: one job per composable.

### Mutations

- `useAgentUpdate(refs)` should:
  - write core updates to `agents/{uid}`
  - write overlay updates to `apps/{appId}/agents/{uid}` only in tenant mode

### Explicit admin fetch (optional but recommended)

- `useAgentAppProfileFetch(targetAppId, uid)`
  - reads `apps/{targetAppId}/agents/{uid}`
  - used only by operator/admin tooling
  - must not depend on “current runtime app” hydration

## UI routes

- `/console/agent`
  - overview and entry point
  - shows status + CTA link to profile builder

- `/console/agent/profile`
  - profile builder / editor
  - supports create-when-missing via ensure flow

## Consistency checks (definition of done)

- Agent model file follows the same structural pattern as Chef/Supplier/Professional.
- `useAgentInterface` is the single source for pill/cell/profile view models.
- `useProfileFetch` gating remains canonical:
  - domain overlays only read in tenant mode
- `apps/{appId}/users/{uid}` remains membership-only (role/notifications), not a proxy for tenant mode.

## Next implementation steps

1. Confirm Agent model matches the Chef/Supplier/Professional shape (types + naming).
2. Ensure the Agent editor writes to the right document(s) via `useAgentUpdate`.
3. Add an explicit admin overlay fetch helper (target app id) if operator tooling needs it.
4. Add one directory/list view that uses `resolveAgentCell`/`pillProps` (via `useAgentInterface`) as the canonical mapping.

## Guardrails (paste into future Copilot prompts)

You are editing FireUX. Follow canon strictly:

- Do NOT mix AppUser membership overlay with domain profile overlays.
  - AppUser: apps/{appId}/users/{uid} is membership/roles/notifications only.
  - Domain profile: agents/{uid} is canonical truth.
  - Tenant delta: apps/{tenantAppId}/agents/{uid} only read/write when isTenant === true unless explicitly admin-fetched by targetAppId.

- Keep model files SHAPE-FIRST:
  - Domain wrapper { user, core, app }
  - Card namespace (ProfileCore/ProfileApp) if used elsewhere
  - NO UI props in model files.

- View models only in useAgentInterface (pill/cell/profile).
- Writes only in useAgentUpdate.
- Creation/ensure only in useAgentCreate or useProfileEnsure.

- Do not add extra entities, deep nesting, or new collections unless required.
- Keep changes minimal and consistent with Chef/Supplier/Professional patterns.

```

### temp/app-user-profile-stack.md

```md
# App / User / Profile stack paths (canon snapshot)

## Core Firestore composables (canon)

- App domain (`packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/composables/fireux/firestore/core/app`)
  - `fetch/`: `useAppCollection.ts`, `useAppFetch.ts`, `useAppUsers.ts`
  - `mutations/`: `useAppDelete.ts`, `useAppEnsure.ts`, `useAppUpdate.ts`
  - `utils/`: `useAppJoinRequests.ts`, `validation/`, `view/`
  - Root: `useApp.ts`
- Profile domain (`packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/composables/fireux/firestore/core/profile`)
  - `fetch/`: `useProfileCollection.ts`, `useProfileFetch.ts`
  - `mutations/`: `useProfileDelete.ts`, `useProfileEnsure.ts`, `useProfileUpdate.ts`
  - `utils/`: `view/`
  - Root: `useProfile.ts`
- User domain (`packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/composables/fireux/firestore/core/user`)
  - `fetch/`: `useUserCollection.ts`, `useUserFetch.ts`
  - `mutations/`: `useAppUserUpdate.ts`, `useCoreUserEnsure.ts`, `useCoreUserUpdate.ts`, `useUserDelete.ts`, `useUserEnsure.ts`, `useUserUpdate.ts`
  - `utils/`: `ensureHelpers.ts`, `validation/`, `view/`
  - Root: `useUser.ts`
- Shared state helper
  - `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/composables/fireux/firestore/state/useProfileState.ts` (generic keyed state helper for profiles)

## Components (app/user/profile-related)

- Core app/profile UI
  - `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/components/layouts/console/ProfilesMenu.vue`
  - `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/components/layouts/console/ProfileEdit.vue`
  - `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/components/organisms/Console/Profile/Edit/Profile.vue`
  - `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/components/organisms/App/Cards/Profile.vue`
  - `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/components/organisms/User/Cards/Profile.vue`
  - Dev aid: `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/components/dev/ProfileDiffList.vue`

## Quick align notes

- Canon already matches core pattern: `fetch/`, `mutations/`, `utils/`, root `use<App|Profile|User>.ts`.
- No `state/` folder yet; add if/when we introduce local draft form state for app/profile/user.
- View/validation live under `utils/`; keep exporting through each root to preserve single entrypoint imports.

```

### temp/cannon-components.md

```md
# Cannon components (components only)

Canon rules (components-only index)
- All profiles live under: `components/organisms/profiles/<Domain>/...`
- All objects live under: `components/organisms/objects/<Object>/...`
- Every profile has: `CTA`, `Preview`, `Profile`, `Create/System`, `Edit/{Core,App,Preview}`, `Cards/{Pill,Cell}`, `Sections/{GlobalCollection,LocalCollection}`
- Every object has at minimum: `Create/System` (and when it’s browsable: `CTA` + `Cards/*`; optionally `List`, `Profile`, `Sections/*`)
- `Pill` is mandatory wherever the object/profile is browsable
- No component paths outside `organisms/**` belong in this doc

Note: `fireux-core` App currently has no `CTA.vue` (accepted).

---

### temp/checklist.md

```md
# FireUX Core Tasks — Checklist

We work **chunk by chunk**. No jobs/roles until core is green.

---

## Chunk 2 — Navigation Reliability + Escape Hatches

### Status (so far)
- ✅ Sign out reliability improved (canonical sign out + console guard)
- ✅ Console has a visible Home escape hatch (one click → `/`)
- ✅ Menu button wiring corrected (avoid duplicate burgers on mobile)
- ✅ Menu reliability validated (tests #1–#6 PASS)

### Definition of “PASS” (binary)
For every test below:
- **PASS** = opens on first click + navigates on first click
- **FAIL** = needs refresh / second click / only works after auth resolves

### Tests
1. **Menu reliability (fresh load)**
   - Fresh load → click menu (desktop)
   - Fresh load → click menu (mobile)
   - Logged out → menu opens + navigates
   - Logged in → menu opens + navigates

2. **No refresh ever required**
   - If any case requires refresh → record:
     - desktop or mobile
     - logged in or out
     - first load or after navigation

3. **Home escape hatch**
   - Visible from all `/console/**` pages
   - Works on desktop and mobile
   - One click → `/`

   Done:
   - Implemented Home button in console layout using `router.replace('/')`

4. **Escape hatch verification**
   - Click Home from console → arrives at `/`
   - Browser Back does not trap user in console

   To verify:
   - Confirm Home is visible on all `/console/**` pages
   - Confirm Back does not bounce back into console after clicking Home

5. **Re-test sign out after navigation changes**
   - Desktop sign out
   - Mobile sign out
   - Refresh after sign out

   Done:
   - Sign out now redirects deterministically (console → `/`, auth surfaces → `/auth`)

   To verify:
   - Sign in → navigate around console → sign out → refresh → still signed out

6. **Menu reliability after first route change (common failure)**
   - Fresh load → open menu → navigate once → open menu again → navigate again
   - Run on:
     - desktop (logged out + logged in)
     - mobile (logged out + logged in)

---

### Stop Condition (Chunk 2)
Do not proceed until:
- Menu works every time
- Home is always reachable
- No refresh required for navigation

### Plan (Chunk 2)
1. Run tests in #1 on fresh load
2. Record any failures for #2
3. Validate #3 is present on all console pages
4. Validate #4 back-button behavior
5. Re-run #5 sign out checks
6. Run #6 (after first route change)
7. Declare “Chunk 2 done” or report the failing number(s)

---

## Chunk 3 — Profile vs Settings (Platform Rule)

### Goal
Clear separation between:
- **Profile** = public identity (avatar, display name, handle, bio)
- **Settings** = private account controls (email, password, privacy, subscription)

### Tasks
1. Ensure navigation labels clearly separate **Profile** and **Settings**
2. Remove ambiguity where “name” can be edited in multiple places
3. Enforce “no silent failures” for any update action:
   - success confirmation OR visible error message

### Stop Condition (Chunk 3)
- A user always knows where to edit public identity vs account settings
- No profile/settings action fails silently

---

## Chunk 4 — Console Core Hygiene

### Tasks
1. Remove dev language from user-facing UI (e.g. “production mode”)
2. Fix greeting fallback:
   - If name exists → “Hello {name}”
   - Else → “Hello”
3. Replace dead buttons:
   - Working link OR disabled with “Coming soon”
4. Console must not assume profiles exist

### Stop Condition (Chunk 4)
- No dev messaging on end-user surfaces
- No dead clicks on console home

---

## Chunk 5 — Zero States → Meaningful Actions

### Tasks
1. Replace meaningless “0 stats” blocks with CTAs:
   - Browse X / Create X
2. Followers/products empty states must be actionable (not just “0”)
3. Any stat shown must answer: “what can I do next?”

### Stop Condition (Chunk 5)
- No “0 followers / 0 purchases / 0 favourites” shown without a next action

---

## Next Quick Wins (no help needed)
1. Run a focused menu reliability pass on FireUX
2. If menu needs refresh: locate the first broken click and fix root cause
3. Ensure mobile menu opens + navigates without refresh
4. Ensure desktop sidebar collapse/menu interactions work first-load
5. Declare Chunk 2 done only when tests #1–#6 pass

```

### temp/console/overview.md

```md
# Console Overview (temp)

Scope: http://localhost:3000/console

This doc is for the *console overview page* (the “Overview” tab).
It is intentionally separate from user-profile editing.

---

## 1) Page + composition

Page:
- packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/pages/console/index.vue

The page renders three layers in order:
1) Core overview (FireUX-wide)
2) Ecosystem overview (e.g. FireUX / Misebox / Cleanbox)
3) App overview (e.g. fireux-app / tenant / niederhorn)

As of the restructuring, each layer is future-proofed under an `overview/` path segment.

---

## 2) Component resolution (what should render)

Core (always from fireux-core):
- packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/components/console/overview/Core.vue

Ecosystem (overridden by the active ecosystem package when available):
- packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/components/console/overview/Ecosystem.vue (fallback)
- packages/ecosystem/<ecosystem>/src/runtime/components/console/overview/Ecosystem.vue (override)

App (overridden by the active app when available):
- packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/components/console/overview/App.vue (fallback)
- projects/<ecosystem>/<app>/app/components/Console/overview/App.vue (override)

We currently keep a visible marker in each component like:
- "Component: ConsoleOverview…" 
so it’s obvious which component is being used.

---

## 3) What belongs in Overview (rules)

Overview should answer:
- “What’s my status right now?”
- “What should I do next?”
- “What changed recently?”

Keep it lightweight:
- small stats, small previews, a few calls-to-action
- no deep settings/editor UIs (those live elsewhere)

---

## 4) Data sources (allowed)

Core user doc:
- /users/{uid}

App membership overlay:
- /apps/{appId}/users/{uid}

Apps list:
- /apps collection

Logo priority used by console ecosystem lists:
1) per-user overrides in user.apps (untyped override bucket)
2) branding URLs on /apps/{appId}

---

## 5) Next planned steps (overview-first)

Near-term (overview):
- Confirm the correct component renders for each ecosystem and app.
- Keep the marker text while wiring is being validated.
- Only after wiring is correct, start implementing the actual overview content.

```

### temp/console/users.md

```md
# Console User Profile (temp)

Scope: http://localhost:3000/console/user-profile

This doc is for the *user profile editing* experience.
We are parking this for now while we build the Overview first.

---

## 1) What this page should be responsible for

User-profile should cover:
- Editing identity fields (display name, avatar, handle, etc.)
- Editing bio/about
- Potentially managing user-level preferences

It should NOT try to become the console overview (no “cards”, no app lists).

---

## 2) Canonical user record

Primary Firestore doc:
- /users/{uid}

Relevant fields (high-level):
- id
- display_name
- avatar
- handle (optional)
- email (optional)
- bio (optional)
- created_at / updated_at

Membership mirrors (used elsewhere):
- userOf[] (apps the user belongs to)
- adminOf[] (apps the user admins)

Notifications (core):
- notifications[]

---

## 3) App overlay (not edited here)

Per-app membership overlay:
- /apps/{appId}/users/{uid}

Contains:
- role ('user' | 'admin')

This should generally be edited by admin flows, not user-profile.

---

## 4) Notes

We previously had a broader user model write-up in temp/user.md.
That file is now considered “source notes”, and this `temp/console/users.md` is the console-specific view.

```

### temp/interfaces.md

```md
#+#+#+#+#+#+#+#+━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
# Interfaces (useXInterface) — Canon v2
#+#+#+#+#+#+#+#+━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

## Purpose

Define a clean, stable contract between Firestore models and UI components.

`use*Interface` composables map raw data → neutral UI payloads, without awareness of where they are rendered.

App is the reference implementation.

## Core Principles (Locked)

### 1) Interfaces are UI-only mappers

- Firestore models handle:
  - validation
  - persistence
  - permissions
- `use*Interface` handles:
  - mapping entities → display-ready props
- `use*Interface` does not implement:
  - environment knowledge
  - permission logic
  - routing policy (it may emit a canonical `href`, but does not decide access)

### 2) “Card” is the collective concept

- Card = Pill | Cell | Preview | Profile
- Pill / Cell / Preview / Profile are rendering variants
- The interface returns one card payload; variants consume what they need

### 3) One payload powers all cards

Preferred pattern:

- One card payload → used by Pill / Cell / Profile / Preview
- Avoid branching payloads per surface unless absolutely required

### 4) Pages stay thin

- Index pages render: `CTA + Collection/Manager`
- Detail pages (`[id].vue`) render: Profile card
- Pages do not map data; mapping happens in the interface

### 5) Badges are contextual, not intrinsic

- Interfaces always return: `badges: []`
- Badges are injected by:
  - Collection managers
  - Pages
  - Higher-order UI contexts
- Interfaces never compute:
  - roles
  - memberships
  - status labels
  - environment flags

## Canonical Card Payload Contract

This is the only required payload an interface must return.

```ts
export interface CardPayload {
  title: string
  subtitle: string
  image: string
  href: string
  badges: string[] // always present; injected later by environment
}
```

Rules:

- No initials
- No IDs
- No permissions
- No memberships
- No derived environment state

## Decision (Locked): no `pill.model` (or `cell.model`, `profile.model`)

- Pill is a visual primitive, not a domain model.
- The contract is convention (and optionally component-local typing), not a shared inheritance tree.
- Interfaces return plain objects that match what the primitive consumes.

## Key correction (important)

- There is ONE payload per interface.
- Do not define `XPillProps`, `XCellProps`, `XProfileProps`.
- Do not “spread” between types.
- Rendering variants (Pill / Cell / Preview / Profile) consume what they need.

## Inventory

### Core

#### App (Reference Implementation)

File:

- `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/composables/fireux/firestore/core/app/utils/view/useAppInterface.ts`

Export:

- `useAppInterface(appRef?: Ref<App | null | undefined>)`

Contract (canonical example):

```ts
export function useAppInterface(appRef?: Ref<App | null | undefined>) {
  const card = (target?: App | null): CardPayload => ({
    title: target?.app_name ?? '',
    subtitle: target?.ecosystem ?? '',
    image: target?.img ?? '',
    href: target?.id ? `/apps/${target.id}` : '',
    badges: [],
  })

  return {
    card,
  }
}
```

Notes:

- Interfaces never return `null`
- Missing data → safe fallbacks
- Badge injection happens elsewhere

Used by:

- Detail page: `pages/apps/[id].vue` → passes `card` into Profile
- Collection: `components/organisms/App/Collection/Manager.vue` → passes `card` into Pill
- Composable facade: `useApp()` spreads interface output

#### User

File:

- `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/composables/fireux/firestore/core/user/utils/view/useUserInterface.ts`

Export:

- `useUserInterface(source?: Ref<User | null | undefined> | UserRefs, context?: { runtime?: 'global' | 'tenant'; appId?: string | null })`

Used by:

- Detail page: `pages/users/[id].vue`
- Collection: `components/organisms/User/Collection/Manager.vue`
- Facade: `useUser()`

### Extensions

Blogs:

- `packages/extensions/fireux-blogs/src/runtime/composables/fireux/firestore/blog/utils/view/useBlogInterface.ts`

Jobs:

- `packages/extensions/fireux-jobs/src/runtime/composables/fireux/firestore/jobs/utils/view/useJobInterface.ts`

Products:

- `packages/extensions/fireux-products/src/runtime/composables/fireux/firestore/product/utils/view/useProductInterface.ts`

Places:

- `packages/extensions/fireux-places/src/runtime/composables/fireux/firestore/place/utils/view/usePlacesInterface.ts`

Jobs profiles:

- Agent: `packages/extensions/fireux-jobs/src/runtime/composables/fireux/firestore/profiles/Agent/main/useAgentInterface.ts`
- Professional: `packages/extensions/fireux-jobs/src/runtime/composables/fireux/firestore/profiles/Professional/main/useProfessionalInterface.ts`

### Ecosystem (Misebox)

- Chef: `packages/ecosystem/fireux-misebox/src/runtime/composables/fireux/firestore/profiles/Chef/main/useChefInterface.ts`
- Supplier: `packages/ecosystem/fireux-misebox/src/runtime/composables/fireux/firestore/profiles/Supplier/main/useSupplierInterface.ts`

## Next logical steps (not doing yet)

- Strip badge logic from `useUserInterface`, `useChefInterface`, `useAgentInterface`, etc.
- Move badge decisions into collection managers and page-level adapters.
- Simplify Pill components to render-only.

```

```md
# Places Stack vs “Starter Stack” (FireUX)

Date: 2025-12-29

Purpose: Blog/Products are evolving, so this doc compares Places against a broader sample (Companies + Misebox ecosystem objects) and then defines a **starter object stack template** (an “imaginary canon”) that we can standardize on.

---

## Observed stacks in this repo (not treated as final)

### Companies (clean facade; minimal but consistent)

- Facade:
  - `packages/extensions/fireux-companies/src/runtime/composables/fireux/firestore/company/useCompanies.ts`
- Fetch:
  - `.../company/fetch/useCompanyFetch.ts` → `{ companies, company }`
- Mutations:
  - `.../company/mutations/useCompanyCreate.ts`
  - `.../company/mutations/useCompanyUpdate.ts`

Useful bits:
- Facade composes fetch + mutations.
- Doesn’t over-abstract; keeps surface area small.

### Misebox ecosystem objects (pragmatic; direct vuefire)

- Ingredient:
  - `packages/ecosystem/fireux-misebox/src/runtime/composables/fireux/firestore/ingredient/useIngredient.ts`
  - Uses `vuefire` `useCollection/useDocument` directly, has SSR keys, includes normalization.
  - Also has a pure “domain helper” composable `useIngredientFilters.ts`.

- Recipes:
  - `packages/ecosystem/fireux-misebox/src/runtime/composables/fireux/firestore/recipe/useRecipes.ts`
  - Similar: direct `vuefire`, returns `{ all, pending, error }` plus CRUD composables.

Useful bits:
- Clear separation between “fetching” and “domain helper” (filters).
- Returns a standard trio `{ data, pending, error }` that pages/components can depend on.
- Uses SSR keys deliberately.

### Blog/Products (examples only)

- They show patterns we like (facade + `utils/view/*Interface.ts`, split fetch), but we do **not** treat them as final canon.

---

## Starter stack template (proposed canon)

This is the **starter stack** you proposed. We can assume this shape for new things and then *omit optional parts* when an object doesn’t need them.

```
src/runtime/
  models/
    objects/
      <Object>.model.ts

  composables/
    fireux/
      firestore/
        objects/
          <object>/
            use<Objects>.ts

            fetch/
              use<Object>Collection.ts
              use<Object>Read.ts
              use<Object>Search.ts

            mutations/
              use<Object>Create.ts
              use<Object>Update.ts
              use<Object>Delete.ts

            state/
              use<Object>DraftState.ts
              use<Object>CreateSubmit.ts
              use<Object>UpdateSubmit.ts

            view/
              use<Object>Interface.ts

  components/
    organisms/
      objects/
        <Object>/
          CTA.vue

          List.vue
          Profile.vue

          Cards/
            Pill.vue
            Cell.vue
            Profile.vue

          Sections/
            GlobalCollection.vue
            LocalCollection.vue

          Create/
            System.vue
            Write.vue
            Preview.vue

          Edit/
            System.vue
            Core.vue
            App.vue
            Preview.vue
```

### Starter rules (required vs optional)

Required (baseline):
- `use<Objects>.ts` is the entry point.
- `fetch/use<Object>Collection.ts` exists (even if it’s tiny).
- `mutations/` exists if the object is editable.
- `view/use<Object>Interface.ts` exists when there are UI cards/cells; components import UI shapes from here (not from models).

Optional (only when needed):
- `fetch/use<Object>Read.ts` (only if you have a single-doc page or doc-level reads).
- `fetch/use<Object>Search.ts` (only if search exists).
- `state/` (only if create/edit UX is multi-step or needs draft state).
- `Sections/GlobalCollection.vue` + `LocalCollection.vue` (only if tenant/global duality exists).
- `Edit/Core.vue` + `Edit/App.vue` (only if the data model truly has split write scopes).

Placement rules:
- `models/objects/<Object>.model.ts` is *data shape* only.
- `view/use<Object>Interface.ts` is UI shape + mapping only (no firestore/network).
- Provider integrations (Google, Stripe, etc.) live under `fetch/<provider>/...` while they’re domain-owned.
- Prefer consistent fetch outputs: `items|collection`, `pending`, `error`.

---

## Places vs the proposed starter stack

### Current Places stack (mapped to the starter shape)

Repo paths today (FireUX mono conventions):
- Data model (not yet under `models/objects/`):
  - `packages/extensions/fireux-places/src/runtime/models/place.model.ts`
- Entry point:
  - `packages/extensions/fireux-places/src/runtime/composables/fireux/firestore/place/usePlaces.ts`
- Fetch:
  - `.../place/fetch/usePlaceCollection.ts` (collectionPath + collection + count)
  - `.../place/fetch/search/usePlacesSearch.ts` (search orchestration)
  - `.../place/fetch/google/usePlacesGoogle.ts` (provider fetch)
- Mutations:
  - `.../place/mutations/usePlaceCreate.ts`
  - `.../place/mutations/usePlaceSave.ts`
- View:
  - `.../place/utils/view/usePlacesInterface.ts` (UI shapes + `toCell()`)
  - `.../place/utils/view/usePlaceLogos.ts` (logo hydration)
- Domain utils:
  - `.../place/utils/placeCollections.ts` (runtimeConfig types → collection mapping)

### Alignment status vs starter

- ✅ Entry point exists at object root (`usePlaces.ts`).
- ✅ Fetch/mutations/view layers exist.
- ✅ UI components can import UI shapes/mappers from `view/usePlacesInterface.ts`.

Gaps (against the starter stack):
- ⚠️ Model placement: Places uses `runtime/models/place.model.ts`; starter wants `runtime/models/Place.model.ts`.
- ⚠️ Model contents: `place.model.ts` still includes UI-ish types/mappers (`PlaceCard`, `toCell`). Starter wants those only in `view/use<Object>Interface.ts`.
- ⚠️ Fetch shape: `usePlaceCollection` returns `collection` (possibly `undefined`) and `count`, but does not expose a first-class `pending` + `error` pair like Misebox’s patterns.
- ⚠️ Naming: we currently use `utils/view/usePlacesInterface.ts` rather than `view/usePlaceInterface.ts` directly under the object. Starter template puts `view/` alongside `fetch/` and `mutations/`.

Notes:
- The repo’s existing canon also uses `utils/view/` in some stacks. Your starter template prefers `view/` at the same level as `fetch/`.
- If we adopt your starter template, we should normalize future objects to `objects/<object>/view/` (and keep a small compatibility window while we migrate older stacks).

---

## Decision point: where should Google Places logic live?

Starter default:
- Keep it domain-owned under `objects/place/fetch/google/*`.

Only elevate to `composables/fireux/integrations/google/places/*` if:
- 2+ non-Place domains need to import the integration client directly.

---

## Next steps to converge Places to the starter stack

1) Make fetch shape consistent
- Add `pending` + `error` style outputs for `usePlaceCollection` (even if `error` is null for now).

2) Continue UI interface migration
- Any UI component needing Place card/cell shapes should import from `utils/view/usePlacesInterface`.

3) Optional: add a thin fetch facade
- `fetch/usePlaceFetch.ts` (if we want a single fetch entry like Company/Blog).

```

```md
# Index canon feasibility (FireUX)

Date: 2025-12-29
Scope: runtime pages + runtime components only (no docs besides this file).

## Summary (worth doing now?)
Yes — a partial rollout is worth doing now.

Why:
- The repo already has the building blocks (CTA components, Preview components, and `Sections/*Collection.vue` components), but index pages still contain orchestration logic (toggles, tenant/global rules, debug panels).
- Standardising the composition to `Header + CTA + CollectionManager` reduces duplication and makes it easier to keep UX consistent across domains.
- This can be rolled out incrementally (domain-by-domain) with minimal risk by adding wrapper organisms first, then simplifying pages.

Why not “full rewrite” right now:
- Some pages (e.g. Professionals) include debug panels and extra toggles that need careful preservation.
- Some CTAs are currently hidden at the index level; moving gating inside CTA components is a UX decision that should be made intentionally.

## 1) Canon term decision: **Collection**
Pick: **Collection** (single term).

Justification:
- The UI is driven by Firestore collections (e.g. `/users`, `/apps`, `/places`, domain-specific collections).
- The repo already uses the term in component names: `*Collection.vue`, `Sections/*Collection.vue`, and “Collection Manager” maps naturally to “owns local/global sections + list rendering”.
- “Directory” is used for profile browsing (Agents/Professionals) but it’s a specialized *kind* of collection view; keeping one canon term avoids per-domain vocabulary drift.

Naming rule:
- Page-level wrapper should be `CollectionManager`.
- Renderers that actually draw the items can stay `List` / `CardsList` internally, but indexes should not reference them directly once a manager exists.

## 2) Current index patterns (repo scan)

### Objects
- Blog index: packages/extensions/fireux-blogs/src/runtime/pages/blog/index.vue
  - `OrganismsObjectsBlogCTA v-if="canPublishBlog"`
  - `OrganismsObjectsBlogList`

- Products index: packages/extensions/fireux-products/src/runtime/pages/products/index.vue
  - `OrganismsObjectsProductCTA v-if="showCTA"`
  - `OrganismsObjectsProductCardsList`

- Jobs index: packages/extensions/fireux-jobs/src/runtime/pages/jobs/index.vue
  - `OrganismsObjectsJobCTA v-if="coreProfile"`
  - `OrganismsObjectsJobSectionsAgentCollection v-if="coreProfile"`
  - `OrganismsObjectsJobSectionsGlobalCollection`

- Places index: packages/extensions/fireux-places/src/runtime/pages/places/index.vue
  - CTA-like organism: `OrganismsObjectsPlaceSearchSection` (not named CTA)
  - List organism: `OrganismsObjectsPlaceList` (prop-driven)

### Profiles / directories
- Agents index: packages/extensions/fireux-jobs/src/runtime/pages/agents/index.vue
  - `OrganismsProfilesAgentPreview`
  - `OrganismsProfilesAgentSectionsLocalCollection v-if="isTenant"`
  - toggle + `OrganismsProfilesAgentSectionsGlobalCollection`

- Professionals index: packages/extensions/fireux-jobs/src/runtime/pages/professionals/index.vue
  - `OrganismsProfilesProfessionalPreview`
  - local collection gated by computed `showLocalDirectory`
  - toggle for global collection
  - debug panel (raw JSON + clipboard)

### Core
- Users index: packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/pages/users/index.vue
  - `OrganismsUserPreview`
  - toggle for global directory
  - `OrganismsUserCollection`

- Apps index: packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/pages/apps/index.vue
  - `OrganismsAppPreview`
  - `OrganismsAppCollection`

### Also present (ecosystem packages)
These follow the same “Preview + LocalCollection + GlobalCollection + toggle” pattern:
- packages/ecosystem/fireux-misebox/src/runtime/pages/chefs/index.vue
- packages/ecosystem/fireux-misebox/src/runtime/pages/suppliers/index.vue

## 3) Existing organisms we can reuse (no guessing)

### CTAs
- Blog CTA component: packages/extensions/fireux-blogs/src/runtime/components/organisms/objects/Blog/CTA.vue
  - CTA is also conditional inside the component (`UPageCTA v-if="showCTA"`).
- Product CTA component: packages/extensions/fireux-products/src/runtime/components/organisms/objects/Product/CTA.vue
  - CTA conditional inside component (`UPageCTA v-if="showCTA"`).
- Job CTA component: packages/extensions/fireux-jobs/src/runtime/components/organisms/objects/Job/CTA.vue
  - Branches internally: shows `OrganismsProfilesAgentCTA` if missing agent profile, else shows “Post a job” CTA.

### Lists / collections / sections
- Blog list: packages/extensions/fireux-blogs/src/runtime/components/organisms/objects/Blog/List.vue
- Products cards list: packages/extensions/fireux-products/src/runtime/components/organisms/objects/Product/Cards/List.vue
- Places list: packages/extensions/fireux-places/src/runtime/components/organisms/objects/Place/List.vue
- Jobs sections collections:

  - packages/extensions/fireux-jobs/src/runtime/components/organisms/objects/Job/Sections/GlobalCollection.vue
- Profile sections collections:
  - packages/extensions/fireux-jobs/src/runtime/components/organisms/profiles/Agent/Sections/{LocalCollection,GlobalCollection}.vue
  - packages/extensions/fireux-jobs/src/runtime/components/organisms/profiles/Professional/Sections/{LocalCollection,GlobalCollection}.vue

### Previews
- Agent preview: packages/extensions/fireux-jobs/src/runtime/components/organisms/profiles/Agent/Preview.vue
  - Already contains conditional “create profile” CTA inside.
- Core previews:
  - packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/components/organisms/User/Preview.vue
  - packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/components/organisms/App/Preview.vue

## 4) Proposed canon names + new wrapper components

### Objects
For each object domain:

- `components/organisms/objects/<Domain>/CollectionManager.vue`

### Core

## 5) Page updates (exact file paths)

Update these pages to become lean:

- Blog:
  - packages/extensions/fireux-blogs/src/runtime/pages/blog/index.vue
    - Target:
      - `<OrganismsObjectsBlogCTA />`
      - `<OrganismsObjectsBlogCollectionManager />`

- Professionals:

### temp/report.md

```md
# FireUX Runtime Plugin + Firebase SSR/TS Diagnostics Report

Date: 2025-12-19

## 1) Observed errors (exact text)

### VS Code / TypeScript diagnostics

In packages/core runtime plugin:

- `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/plugins/firebase.client.ts`
  - Previously:
    - `Module '"#imports"' has no exported member 'defineNuxtPlugin'.`
    - `Module '"#imports"' has no exported member 'useRuntimeConfig'.`
  - Current status: **fixed** by extending the repo Nuxt shims so package-context runtime plugins can import these helpers from `#imports`.

(Other runtime plugins that import from `#imports`, e.g. `fireux-config.*` and `inject-trace.*`, currently typecheck without errors.)

### Terminal (Nuxt dev/prepare)

Not captured in this run. Use the commands in section 5 to capture reproducible terminal output.

## 2) Current architecture summary (brief)

- Env vars are read in: `packages/core/fireux-core/src/config/app/fireux.config.ts`
  - Reads `process.env.APP_DOMAIN`, `NUXT_FIREBASE_APP_ID`, `NUXT_FIREBASE_MEASUREMENT_ID`, `DEVELOPER_PIN`.

- runtimeConfig is set in: `packages/core/fireux-core/src/config/app/runtime.ts`
  - `setRuntime()` writes to `runtimeConfig.public.fireux`, `runtimeConfig.public.firebaseEcosystem`, `runtimeConfig.public.firebaseApp`.
  - It supports both a NuxtConfig object (`nuxt.runtimeConfig`) and a Nuxt instance (`nuxt.options.runtimeConfig`) by using `(nuxt.options ?? nuxt)`.

- Ecosystem config injects firebase ecosystem in: `packages/ecosystem/fireux-*/src/module.ts`
  - Example: `packages/ecosystem/fireux-fireux/src/module.ts` imports its own `./config/firebase/ecosystem.config` and calls `setRuntimeFirebaseEcosystem(...)`.

- VueFire is configured in: `packages/core/fireux-core/src/module.ts` (modules:done hook)
  - `modules:done` is used as the safe point because ecosystem modules should have already injected `runtimeConfig.public.firebaseEcosystem` and app config should have injected `runtimeConfig.public.firebaseApp`.
  - `configVuefire(nuxt)` writes a `nuxt.vuefire.config` object based on runtimeConfig.

- Firebase web app initialization lives in: `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/plugins/firebase.client.ts`
  - Uses `firebase/app` (`getApps`, `initializeApp`).
  - Uses `defineNuxtPlugin` + `useRuntimeConfig` via `#imports`.
  - It is registered as client-only by filename (`*.client.ts`) if/when it is injected.

## 3) Tree + key files inspected

### Runtime plugin filenames

Under `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/plugins/`:

- `firebase.client.ts`
- `fireux-config.client.ts`
- `fireux-config.server.ts`
- `inject-trace.client.ts`
- `inject-trace.server.ts`

### Are runtime plugins registered into the consuming app build?

Evidence strongly suggests: **not currently**.

- There is a helper that *would* register them via Nuxt module API:
  - `packages/core/fireux-core/src/config/module/plugins-config.ts` defines `configurePlugins(resolver)` and calls `addPlugin(...)` for each runtime plugin.
- But `packages/core/fireux-core/src/module.ts` does **not** call `configurePlugins(...)` (it only sets an alias and hooks `modules:done` to call `configVuefire`).
- Grepping the consuming app’s `.nuxt` output did not find the plugin injection strings for `firebase.client.ts` / `fireux-config.*` / `inject-trace.*`.
  - `.nuxt` does include tsconfig path aliases pointing at `packages/core/fireux-core/runtime`, which confirms the runtime alias exists, but that does not mean plugins are injected.

Conclusion: right now the repo has the code to inject plugins (`configurePlugins`) but it is not wired in.

## 4) Hypotheses (ranked)

### A. Runtime plugin file is not being registered into the consuming app build (most likely)

- `configurePlugins()` exists but is unused.
- `.nuxt` grep does not show injected plugins.
- This would explain “Firebase init is missing” even if the runtime plugin code is correct.

### B. It runs only on client (`firebase.client.ts`), so SSR doesn’t have a Firebase web app

- Even after plugin injection is fixed, the current Firebase init plugin is client-only.
- If server-side code expects Firebase Web SDK state during SSR, it will still be missing.

### C. Editor TS errors are from missing Nuxt types in the package context

- Partially true in general, but in *this* repo many runtime files import from `#imports` successfully.
- We addressed the concrete `firebase.client.ts` failure by updating `types/nuxt-shims.d.ts` to explicitly declare `defineNuxtPlugin` and `useRuntimeConfig` in the `#imports` module.

### D. `pnpm clean` deleting node_modules causes type resolution confusion

- This can exacerbate editor issues after a clean, but the core root cause for Node typings is configuration: root `tsconfig.json` requests `types: ["nuxt", "node"]` and requires `@types/node` to be installed.

## 5) Verification commands + expected output

### Prove whether plugins are injected into the consuming app

- Search in `.nuxt` for injected plugin paths:

  ```sh
  rg -n "fireux-core/src/runtime/plugins" projects/fireux/fireux-app/.nuxt --hidden --no-ignore
  rg -n "firebase\\.client" projects/fireux/fireux-app/.nuxt --hidden --no-ignore
  rg -n "inject-trace" projects/fireux/fireux-app/.nuxt --hidden --no-ignore
  ```

Expected:
- If plugins are correctly injected, you should see references to the resolved plugin files under `.nuxt` plugin manifests.
- If nothing appears, plugin injection is not wired.

### Prove whether Firebase init runs on server vs client

- Add a temporary log inside the plugin:
  - Client marker: `console.log('[fireux-core/firebase] init', { hasEco: !!eco, hasAppId: !!app?.appId })`
- Then watch:
  - Browser console (client) should show it.
  - Server terminal should *not* show it for `.client.ts`.

### Capture terminal type errors

- Run Nuxt prepare/typecheck for the app:

  ```sh
  pnpm --filter ./projects/fireux/fireux-app exec nuxi prepare
  pnpm --filter ./projects/fireux/fireux-app exec nuxi typecheck
  ```

Expected:
- If plugin injection is broken, `nuxi` output won’t mention those plugins.
- If TS shims are incomplete, you will see `#imports` and `defineNuxtPlugin`-related errors.

## 6) Proposed fix plan (smallest steps first)

### Step 1 — Wire plugin registration (required)

- In `packages/core/fireux-core/src/module.ts`, call `configurePlugins(resolver)`.
- This makes runtime plugins actually enter the consuming app build.

### Step 2 — Fix the concrete TS error in firebase plugin (required)

Current status: **done**.

- `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/plugins/firebase.client.ts` imports `defineNuxtPlugin` and `useRuntimeConfig` from `#imports`.
- `types/nuxt-shims.d.ts` explicitly declares those exports for package-context typechecking.

### Step 3 — Decide SSR strategy for Firebase (smallest safe approach)

Two viable options:

- **Option A (minimal + safe): keep Firebase Web init client-only**
  - Keep `firebase.client.ts` for browser Firebase Web SDK.
  - Ensure any server-side Firestore usage goes through `firebase-admin` (Nitro server routes already exist in core runtime).
  - Add guardrails in server-side composables so they don’t assume a Web SDK app exists.

- **Option B (matches preference “universal plugin”): add a universal plugin but no-op on server**
  - Create `firebase.ts` (universal) that checks `import.meta.server` / `process.server` and returns early on server.
  - Net effect: one plugin path, SSR-safe (no server crash), but still only initializes Web SDK on client.

(Actually initializing Firebase Web SDK during SSR is generally not needed; server code should prefer admin SDK.)

### Exact file edits (summary)

1) `packages/core/fireux-core/src/module.ts`
- Import `configurePlugins` and call it in `setup()`.

2) `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/plugins/firebase.client.ts`
- Add `import { defineNuxtPlugin, useRuntimeConfig } from '#imports'`.
- (Optional) adjust header comment to match filename.

---

## Notes

- The repo already has tsconfig shims that map `#imports` (see root `types/nuxt-shims.d.ts` referenced by `paths` in `tsconfig.base.json`), which is why most runtime files can typecheck outside a generated `.nuxt/types` context.
- The remaining missing type definitions error for `node` is solved by installing `@types/node` (root `tsconfig.json` requests it via `compilerOptions.types`).

```

# CTA Inventory (Runtime)

Repo-truth snapshot (runtime only) focused on the **CTA surface** (`UPageCTA`).

- Included `CTA.vue` files: 9
- Last updated: 2025-12-31

This file has two goals:
1) **Current state**: what each CTA renders today.
2) **Desired state**: the lean/clean canon we want across entities and objects.

---

## Current state

### Core — App CTA

Path: `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/components/organisms/App/CTA.vue`

Pattern: **Ensure/Create CTA** (preview only when ready)

```vue
<UPageCTA
  title="Current app"
  description="The app currently resolved for this runtime."
  variant="naked"
>
  <template #default>
    <OrganismsAppCardsPreview v-if="isResolved && isInitialized" />
    <OrganismsAppCreateSystem v-else />
    <UButton variant="ghost" size="sm" to="/learn-more">Learn more</UButton>
  </template>
</UPageCTA>

// state: const { isResolved, isInitialized } = useApp()
```

Notes:
- Preview is **inside** the CTA surface.
- Preview is **pessimistic** (requires `isResolved && isInitialized`).
- Create/System owns the flow.

### Core — User CTA

Path: `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/components/organisms/User/CTA.vue`

  <OrganismsUserCreateSystem v-else />
</UPageCTA>

```md
# FireUX User — field map + relationships (temp)

Console-specific notes now live in:
- temp/console/overview.md (for /console)
- temp/console/users.md (for /console/user-profile)

Goal: give a practical rundown of what a **User** is in this repo, which Firestore docs it touches, and how it relates to Apps / AppUsers / Profiles so you can ideate a richer console.

This is based on:
- [packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/models/core/user.model.ts](packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/models/core/user.model.ts)
- user fetch/ensure/update helpers under `packages/core/fireux-core/src/runtime/composables/fireux/firestore/core/user/`

---

## 1) Core identity: `/users/{uid}` (canonical)

The canonical user record lives at:
- Firestore doc: `/users/{uid}`
- Model: `User`

### `User` fields (current)

Required:
- `id: string`
- `display_name: string`
- `avatar: string`
- `created_at: FirebaseTimestamp`

Optional identity:
- `handle?: string`
- `email?: string`
- `bio?: string`
- `updated_at?: FirebaseTimestamp`

Membership:
- `profiles?: string[]`
- `userOf?: string[]` — array of app IDs the user belongs to
- `adminOf?: string[]` — array of app IDs the user admins

Tenant overlay (computed/attached at runtime):
- `role?: 'user' | 'admin'` — not always stored on the core doc; may be derived from app overlay
- `appUser?: AppUser | null` — the app-scoped overlay doc (see below)

Notifications:
- `notifications?: UserNotification[]`

### Notes on how it’s used
- The UI often treats `User` as “the thing to render”, even in tenant mode.
- In tenant mode, the app overlay may override role: see the merge in `useUserFetch`.

---

## 2) App-scoped membership overlay: `/apps/{appId}/users/{uid}`

This is the per-app overlay that tracks the user’s role *inside* an app.

- Firestore doc: `/apps/{appId}/users/{uid}`
- Model: `AppUser`

### `AppUser` fields (current)
- `id: string` (same as uid)
- `role: 'user' | 'admin'`
- `creator_id: string` (who created/added this membership)
- `created_at: FirebaseTimestamp`
- `updated_at?: FirebaseTimestamp`
- `notifications?: UserNotification[]` (app-scoped)

### How it relates to `/users/{uid}`
- The core doc mirrors membership IDs in arrays (`userOf`, `adminOf`).
- The app overlay doc is the source of truth for app-local role and app-local notifications.
- In runtime, `useUserFetch` merges these:
  - if only core exists: returns core
  - if core + appUser exist: returns `{ ...core, role: appUser.role ?? core.role, appUser }`

---

## 3) Notifications: user-level and app-level

Model:
- `NotificationScope = 'ecosystem' | 'app'`
- `UserNotification`:
  - `id`, `message`, `scope`, `created_at`
  - `read?: boolean`
  - `app_id?: string` (used when `scope: 'app'`)

Write paths:
- Core notification push writes into `/users/{uid}.notifications` using `arrayUnion`.
  - Implemented in `useCoreUserUpdate().notifications.push(...)`.
- Membership ensure flows also push notifications when joining apps.

Console ideas this enables:
- “What changed since last visit?” stream
- “You joined X”, “You were promoted to admin”, “New onboarding step”
- scoped filtering (ecosystem vs app)

---

## 4) Profiles: user ties to other entity collections

You have a dedicated **Profile domain** in core. Profiles are separate entities (e.g. domain-specific records) that reference a user.

Where profiles can live:
- Global: `/{collectionName}/{profileId}`
- Tenant-local: `/apps/{appId}/{collectionName}/{profileId}`

How user resolution works:
- `useProfileCollection` hydrates profiles with a user display snapshot.
- It pulls user info from:
  1) the enriched user collection for the active app (`useUserCollection`) and
  2) falls back to direct core lookups in `/users/{uid}`.

Console ideas this enables:
- show “your profiles” across domains (jobs, places, products, etc.)
- show “profiles missing info” or “profiles you own/admin”

---

## 5) Membership mechanics: how a user joins apps

Conceptually there are three linked things:

1) `/apps/{appId}`
- has governance fields like `admin_ids` and `join_requests`

2) `/apps/{appId}/users/{uid}`
- the per-app membership overlay (`AppUser`)

3) `/users/{uid}`
- mirrors membership IDs in `userOf` / `adminOf`

The ensure helper `ensureUserAppMembership(...)` performs:
- create `/apps/{appId}/users/{uid}` if missing
- ensure `/users/{uid}` exists
- update `/users/{uid}.userOf` and possibly `.adminOf`
- optionally push a notification

Admin promotion/demotion cascades:
- `useAppUserUpdate` and `useAppUpdate` update:
  - `/apps/{appId}/users/{uid}.role`
  - `/apps/{appId}.admin_ids`
  - `/users/{uid}.adminOf` (mirror)

---

## 6) Role resolution (global vs tenant)

There are effectively **two role concepts**:

- **Global role** (ecosystem-wide): stored on `/users/{uid}.role` sometimes
- **Tenant role** (within an app): stored in `/apps/{appId}/users/{uid}.role`

The UI helpers resolve admin status roughly like:
- If global runtime: user is admin if `user.role === 'admin'` OR `adminOf` is non-empty
- If tenant runtime: user is admin if `appUser.role === 'admin'` OR user is in `adminOf` for active `appId`

Console ideas this enables:
- show admin-only modules/CTA
- show “you are admin of X apps” badge

---

## 7) The “user.apps” branding overrides (console logos)

Some console components treat `user.apps` as an *optional* per-user override bucket.

Important: `user.apps` is **not typed in the `User` interface** right now; it’s accessed as an untyped field.

Shapes supported by UI code:
- object map: `user.apps[appId] = { avatar_url | logo_url | wordmark_url | ... }`
- array form: `user.apps = [ { id/app_id/appId: '...', avatar_url/logo_url/... }, ... ]`

Usage:
- used to override app branding for the current user (e.g. custom avatar/logo)
- falls back to `apps/{appId}.avatar_url/logo_url/wordmark_url` if not present

Console ideas:
- per-user “favorite app icon” / “pin” / “hide”
- per-user “custom label” or “grouping” for apps

---

## 8) Summary diagram

- `/users/{uid}` (User)
  - identity + membership mirrors + notifications
  - `userOf[]` / `adminOf[]` reference app IDs
  - `profiles[]` references profile IDs (or tag-like IDs) depending on conventions

- `/apps/{appId}` (App)
  - contains `admin_ids[]`, `join_requests[]`, and branding urls

- `/apps/{appId}/users/{uid}` (AppUser)
  - per-app role + per-app notifications

- `/{profilesCollection}/{profileId}` and `/apps/{appId}/{profilesCollection}/{profileId}` (Profile)
  - encourages “user as owner” relationships via `profile.user.id` (or profile ID == uid)

---

## 9) “Rich user” idea prompts (based on existing primitives)
```

```js
const vscode = require('vscode')
const cp = require('node:child_process')
const fs = require('node:fs')
const path = require('node:path')

function execFileAsync(cmd, args, { maxBuffer } = {}) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    cp.execFile(cmd, args, { maxBuffer: maxBuffer ?? 1024 * 1024 }, (err, stdout, stderr) => {
      if (err) {
        err.stdout = stdout
        err.stderr = stderr
        reject(err)
        return
      }
      resolve({ stdout, stderr })
    })
  })
}

function shellQuotePosix(value) {
  const s = String(value ?? '')
  if (s.length === 0) return "''"
  return `'${s.replaceAll("'", `'\\''`)}'`
}

function cwdForUri(uri) {
  try {
    if (!uri || !uri.fsPath) return undefined
    const fsPath = uri.fsPath
    // Heuristic: if it has an extension, treat as file.
    if (path.extname(fsPath)) return path.dirname(fsPath)
    return fsPath
  } catch {
    return undefined
  }
}

function isProbablyBinary(buffer) {
  if (!buffer || buffer.length === 0) return false
  const limit = Math.min(buffer.length, 8000)
  for (let i = 0; i < limit; i++) {
    if (buffer[i] === 0) return true
  }
  return false
}

function normalizeRelPath(rel) {
  return rel.split(path.sep).join('/')
}

async function collectFilesRecursive(fsApi, rootDir, opts) {
  const ignoreNames = new Set([
    '.git',
    'node_modules',
    'dist',
    '.nuxt',
    '.output',
    '.data',
    '.cache',
    '.nitro',
  ])

  const results = []
  const stack = [rootDir]

  while (stack.length) {
    const dir = stack.pop()
    let entries
    try {
      entries = await fsApi.readDirectory(vscode.Uri.file(dir))
    } catch {
      continue
    }

    for (const [name, type] of entries) {
      if (ignoreNames.has(name)) continue
      if (name === '.DS_Store') continue

      const full = path.join(dir, name)

      if ((type & vscode.FileType.Directory) === vscode.FileType.Directory) {
        stack.push(full)
        continue
      }
      if ((type & vscode.FileType.File) !== vscode.FileType.File) continue

      results.push(full)
      if (results.length >= opts.maxFiles) return results
    }
  }

  return results
}

async function buildCatTreeText(rootDir, { maxFiles, maxFileBytes, maxTotalBytes }) {
  const files = await collectFilesRecursive(vscode.workspace.fs, rootDir, { maxFiles })
  files.sort((a, b) => a.localeCompare(b))

  const decoder = new TextDecoder('utf-8', { fatal: false })
  let total = 0
  const chunks = []

  for (const abs of files) {
    const rel = normalizeRelPath(path.relative(rootDir, abs))
    const header = `\n\n===== ./${rel} =====\n`
    chunks.push(header)
    total += Buffer.byteLength(header, 'utf8')
    if (total > maxTotalBytes) {
      chunks.push('\n[cat-tree truncated: output size exceeded]\n')
      break
    }

    let data
    try {
      data = await vscode.workspace.fs.readFile(vscode.Uri.file(abs))
    } catch {
      chunks.push('[unreadable]\n')
      continue
    }

    if (data.byteLength > maxFileBytes) {
      chunks.push(`[skipped: file too large (${data.byteLength} bytes)]\n`)
      continue
    }

    const buf = Buffer.from(data)
    if (isProbablyBinary(buf)) {
      chunks.push('[skipped: binary file]\n')
      continue
    }

    const text = decoder.decode(buf)
    chunks.push(text)
    total += Buffer.byteLength(text, 'utf8')
    if (total > maxTotalBytes) {
      chunks.push('\n[cat-tree truncated: output size exceeded]\n')
      break
    }
  }

  return chunks.join('')
}

function tryRealpath(absPath) {
  try {
    return fs.realpathSync(absPath)
  } catch {
    return null
  }
}

function formatRealTarget({ workspaceRootDir, realAbsPath }) {
  if (!realAbsPath) return ''
  if (!workspaceRootDir) return normalizeRelPath(realAbsPath)

  const rel = path.relative(workspaceRootDir, realAbsPath)
  if (!rel || rel.startsWith('..') || path.isAbsolute(rel)) {
    return normalizeRelPath(realAbsPath)
  }

  return normalizeRelPath(rel)
}

async function buildMirrorTreeText(
  mirrorDir,
  { workspaceRootDir, maxFiles, maxFileBytes, maxTotalBytes }
) {
  const files = await collectFilesRecursive(vscode.workspace.fs, mirrorDir, { maxFiles })
  const filtered = files.filter((abs) => {
    const base = path.basename(abs)
    if (base === 'README.md') return false
    if (base === 'mirror.txt') return false
    return true
  })
  filtered.sort((a, b) => a.localeCompare(b))

  const decoder = new TextDecoder('utf-8', { fatal: false })
  let total = 0
  const chunks = []

  for (const abs of filtered) {
    const rel = normalizeRelPath(path.relative(mirrorDir, abs))
    const realAbs = tryRealpath(abs)
    const realDisplay = formatRealTarget({ workspaceRootDir, realAbsPath: realAbs })
    const isDifferent = !!(realAbs && path.resolve(realAbs) !== path.resolve(abs))

    const header = `\n\n===== ./${rel}${isDifferent ? ` -> ${realDisplay}` : ''} =====\n`
    chunks.push(header)
    total += Buffer.byteLength(header, 'utf8')
    if (total > maxTotalBytes) {
      chunks.push('\n[mirror-tree truncated: output size exceeded]\n')
      break
    }

    let data
    try {
      data = await vscode.workspace.fs.readFile(vscode.Uri.file(abs))

```ts
// types/nuxt-shims.d.ts
// Global Nuxt shims so packages (like fireux-core, fireux-jobs, fireux-misebox)
// can use Nuxt virtual modules (#imports, #app, #build) without TS/VS Code errors.

declare module '#imports' {
  // Re-export everything Nuxt normally auto-imports
  export * from 'nuxt/app'

  /**
   * Optional: color mode composable used in your core runtime.
   * This is a light-weight type so TS is happy in packages.
   * The actual implementation still comes from your Nuxt modules (@nuxt/ui / color-mode).
   */
  export function useColorMode(): {
    value: string
    preference?: string
    unknown?: boolean
  }

  // Explicit re-export so TS always sees the macro
  export const definePageMeta: typeof import('nuxt/app')['definePageMeta']

  // In some package contexts VS Code/tsserver may not resolve `vue` types.
  // Provide loose shims for common Vue composables used in SFCs.
  export function ref<T = any>(value?: T): any
  export function computed<T = any>(getter: (...args: any[]) => T): any
  export function reactive<T extends object>(value: T): T
  export function watch(...args: any[]): any
  export function watchEffect(...args: any[]): any
  export function onErrorCaptured(...args: any[]): any

  // Common Nuxt composables/macros used across package runtime.
  // Keep these as loose types; real types come from app-generated .nuxt d.ts.
  export function useRoute(...args: any[]): any
  export function useRouter(...args: any[]): any
  export function navigateTo(...args: any[]): any
  export function useHead(...args: any[]): any
  export function useSeoMeta(...args: any[]): any
  export function useToast(...args: any[]): any
  export function useFetch<T = any>(...args: any[]): any
  export function useNuxtApp(...args: any[]): any

  // Minimal shims for package-context runtime plugins.
  // (In real apps these come from Nuxt-generated `#imports` types.)
  export function defineNuxtPlugin(...args: any[]): any
  export function useRuntimeConfig(...args: any[]): any
  export function useRequestEvent(...args: any[]): any
}

// Minimal shim for vuefire server utilities used in package runtime plugins.
declare module 'vuefire/server' {
  export function ensureAdminApp(options?: any): any
}

/**
 * Shim for `#app` so you can import from it in packages
 * (runtime app context, defineNuxtPlugin, etc.)
 */
declare module '#app' {
  export * from 'nuxt/app'
}

/**
 * Shim for `#build` – some Nuxt internals / modules import this.
 * You usually don't need strong typing here, just avoid TS errors.
 */
declare module '#build' {
  const _default: any
  export default _default
}

declare global {
  const definePageMeta: typeof import('nuxt/app')['definePageMeta']
  function useRoute(...args: any[]): any
  function useRouter(...args: any[]): any
  function navigateTo(...args: any[]): any
  function useHead(...args: any[]): any
  function useSeoMeta(...args: any[]): any
  function useFetch<T = any>(...args: any[]): any
  function useAsyncData<T = any>(...args: any[]): any
  function useNuxtApp(...args: any[]): any
}

export {}

### types/vite/client.d.ts

```ts
// Shim for Nuxt-generated `.nuxt/types/builder-env.d.ts` which does `import "vite/client";`.
// This avoids editor/TS resolution issues caused by Vite package `exports`.

interface ImportMetaEnv {
  readonly BASE_URL?: string
  readonly MODE?: string
  readonly DEV?: boolean
  readonly PROD?: boolean
  readonly SSR?: boolean
  readonly [key: string]: string | boolean | undefined
}

interface ImportMeta {
  readonly env: ImportMetaEnv
}

declare module 'vite/client' {
  // The real Vite client types mostly augment global types (ImportMetaEnv).
  // Keeping this module empty is enough for TS to resolve the import.
  export {}
}
